startBasis:
Revised by task 'broth-composition' (2026-08-18, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/broth-composition-report.md; read it in full). The project owner required explicit water at a true liquid density and an honest enrichment factor for the carbon pool; the previous composition (C:6000,O:2000,H:6000,M:200, with no water at all) did not contain the medium the user had asked for ('our medium must be a natural broth').

1. Water density measured, not guessed. Pure water (no C/O/H/M) was run in short probes (3000 steps, box 21σ, kT=1.1) at densities 0.4-0.85 σ⁻³; the quantities measured were largest-void on a coarse 3σ grid (simple presence, not radius) and the dispersion index (variance/mean of the particle count over 27σ³ cells: ~1 for a Poissonian/homogeneous liquid, >>1 for a clumped gas with vacuum bubbles). Result (see the report, table §1): ρ=0.5: 24.5% of the box volume in a single empty cell, dispersion 9.19; ρ=0.65: 10.8%/5.49; ρ=0.7: 4.4%/4.23; ρ=0.72: 10.5%/4.68; ρ=0.75: 5.8%/3.55; ρ=0.78: 6.7%/3.34; ρ=0.8: 0 empty coarse cells/0.207 (sub-Poissonian, homogeneous); ρ=0.85: 0/0.193. The transition "there is a macroscopic void" → "there is none" lies between 0.78 and 0.8. Chosen: 0.8 σ⁻³ as the lowest measured density with no voids and with sub-Poissonian homogeneity, the signature of a liquid, not a gas. Rank D (measured by this task on the specific interaction model, not a literature constant). One water bead remains a coarse-grained representative of ~7-13 real H2O molecules (explicit-water-report.md, §1.1); the project has no σ→nm calibration, the range estimate stays the same, and this task did not refine it.

2. But: 0.8 with the full broth (with catalyst, radiusSigma=1.2, larger than water) was measured to be unstable. The run box=30, {C:1500,O:500,H:1500,M:100,W:21600} (total density 0.9333 σ⁻³) blew up: assertVerletSafety caught a measured drift of 24.58σ against the skin/2=0.75σ bound within the first 10 steps. Not NaN, but a violent, physically unrealistic jump. Diagnosis: the cold jittered start (soup/src/soup-init-state.ts, jitterFrac=0.15) gives a minimum gap of (1-2·0.15)·spacing≈0.7·spacing; at spacing=0.9333⁻¹ᐟ³≈1.023σ this is 0.716σ, less than the catalyst-catalyst contact distance (σ·(1.2+1.2)/2=1.2σ), i.e. some of the starting particles overlap by ~40% of the WCA well depth, which gives a huge but finite force spike. Pure water on its own (without M) at density 0.8 ran stably (see item 1, nonFinite=0 everywhere); the instability is specific to the mixture with the large catalyst at high total density, not a property of water as such. Decision (within the task budget, without reworking the cold-start initialisation, which would be a separate task): the total broth density was lowered to ~0.53 σ⁻³, the same order as this engine has run safely throughout the project (box30, N=14200, ρ=0.526, not a single recorded blow-up over dozens of tasks in the history). Honestly: this means that water's own partial density in the mixture (10700/27000=0.396 σ⁻³) is below the liquid threshold measured in item 1 (0.8σ⁻³). The declared 'liquid' density and the water density actually used in the mixture differ, and this is recorded as a discrepancy, not hidden. Confirmed by measurement: 20000 steps on {C:1500,O:500,H:1500,M:100,W:10700}, box30, kT=1.1: nonFinite=0, no blow-up, listCapacity=2500 (see verletList.basis) did not overflow, throughput≈1907 steps/s.

3. Carbon pool enrichment: an honest number. Literature anchor (Lerman & Groy / review ACS Earth and Space Chem. 2023, "Plausible Sources of Membrane-Forming Fatty Acids on the Early Earth", PMC9869395, already cited in the project specification): a single delivery episode by a carbonaceous meteorite gives ~15 mM of decanoic acid in a concentrated pond (the most generous of the scenarios the review considers, not full dilution across the whole ocean, which would be orders of magnitude lower). Mole fraction relative to pure water (55.5 mol/L): 0.015/55.5≈2.703e-4. Our model 'carbon pool' is C+O (the monomers the amphiphile is physically made of): 1500+500=2000; relative to water 10700: 2000/10700=0.1869. Enrichment factor = 0.1869/2.703e-4 ≈ 691×. This is a conservative (underestimated) figure: the comparison is against the already most generous literature scenario (a pond after meteorite delivery), not against the real dilution across the whole prebiotic ocean, which would be lower by further orders of magnitude. Why enrichment is necessary: without it (at a mole fraction of ~2.7e-4 even in the generous scenario) there would be ~3700 water particles per carbon particle, and that is still not full ocean dilution; separately, this same task measured (see co_bond note below) that even at 691× enrichment the termination reaction (co_bond) did not fire even once in 150000 steps, i.e. at real dilution the reaction would be categorically unreachable within any step budget of this project, not merely slow.

4. O:C left at 1:3 (was 2000:6000, the same ratio); raising the heads was tested and gave no measurable effect. The task explicitly required raising the O fraction to shorten the tails through composition, not through the rate co_bond.attemptRate (which had already been recalibrated many times, see the entries below). Tested (box22, C1500,H1500,M50,W8518, the same water density 0.8 as in item 1): O:C=0.333 and O:C=1.0, up to 150000 steps in the second case. In both cases coBondEvents=0 (ccBondEvents 43-410, growing over time, so chains do grow but are never closed off by a head). Raising O:C from 0.333 to 1.0 did not change a single measurable number (0 amphiphiles in both cases); in this range the composition is statistically indistinguishable by this criterion, so there is no measured reason to change it from the historically established value.

5. The main negative finding of this task: with water, no amphiphile growth is observed. co_bond (a head closing off a chain) did not fire even once at any tested composition (O:C from 0.333 to 1.0) or at any step budget (40000 and 150000): 0 events out of 0 closing attempts, against hundreds of successful cc_bond (chain growth). Diagnosis (not strictly proven; the best explanation within this task's budget): the head (O) is polar and receives a new attraction to water (solvent-polar, added in this explicit-water task), which was absent from every earlier rate calibration (kinetic-growth/surface-growth/adsorption/rate-rederivation/bead-scale-report, all dated 2026-08-17, before explicit-water 2026-08-18). A hydrophilically dissolved head statistically prefers to stay among the water rather than visit the catalytic tip (surrounded by apolar particles: the catalyst and the growing chain), so the frequency of encounters between a head and the growing end collapsed far below the value co_bond.attemptRate=2.562669112 was calibrated for (the calibration fully assumed a world without water). Consequence for the task 'find a composition giving a measured mean tail length of 2-3': this task cannot be accomplished through composition. The measured mean tail length via natural catalysis = undefined (0 amphiphiles), not a number in the range 2-3 and not a number outside it. The bilayer thickness (gate 6) was measured separately with the same method that tests/water-bilayer.test.ts already used: pre-assembled (not grown) lipids with an assumed (not measured by growth) tail length of 2 beads (a convention of this model: a real C12-C18 lipid is already two tail beads); see tests/water-bilayer-broth.test.ts and the report. As the task required ('do NOT tune a potential, do not present a near-miss as a pass'), the rate co_bond.attemptRate was not recomputed again, despite the zero event count found; this is reported as a finding, not cured by fitting yet another number without an independent measurement of the new geometric encounter frequency (which by itself would require a separate GPU campaign, beyond this task's budget).

6. M (catalyst) was raised from its original fraction (200/14200=1.41%) to 100/3600=2.78% relative to the non-biological pool: a pragmatic choice for a reasonable density of synthesis sites at the reduced absolute scale, empirically confirmed as stable (see item 2); it was not re-measured separately from the rest of the stability check.

The old history entries below (O=2000, before this task) are kept untouched as an archive of the reasoning about the minimum number of heads for a vesicle. That arithmetic was for a waterless world and, per item 5, can no longer be reached by natural growth with water in principle, so it is not reused as a current target number, only as historical context.

---

Historical entry (O=2000, before task 'broth-composition'): rank D, a broth composition, not a measured pre-reaction ratio. Measurement (.superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/yield-census-report.md, 45000 steps, kT=1.1, old composition O=900): at least one closed vesicle is needed, by its own area-per-lipid geometry (a≈1.209 σ², t≈4.457 σ); the minimal non-degenerate vesicle requires N≈4π(6.68²+2.23²)/1.209≈516 amphiphiles. Of 900 heads, 614 (68.2%) form no bond at all in 45000 steps: the head 'rank' never enters the reaction; this is co_bond kinetics at the given kT, not a defect of the composition. Arithmetic: to get ~516 heads bonded to anything at all, at least 516/(1-0.682)=516/0.318≈1623 heads are needed, and that is still an optimistic estimate (it does not account for some of the bonded heads attaching somewhere other than the chain end; see the valence report). O=2000 gives a margin above 1623 (≈23%); C/H/M are untouched. This is a choice of what the experiment is able to test (whether the broth can supply enough raw material for a vesicle), not a measured plausible head:tail ratio in the prebiotic soup. In total N=14200 (was 13100, +8.4%), the same order of magnitude; the step rate should not change noticeably.

rules.basis:
estimate: carbon chain growth proceeds only at a catalytic centre; the 6 kT depth sets the chain's resistance to thermal break. Calibration attempt rolled back (task 'energy-calibration', 2026-08-17, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/energy-calibration-report.md; read it in full before trying again): the goal was to bring the mean tail length up to the measured length of real membrane lipids (12-18 carbon atoms) via the Flory relation mean=1/(1-p), p=Kc/(1+Kc), K=exp(energyKT/kT). The arithmetic on paper was correct: from the measured mean=2.086226203807391 at 6 kT/kT=1.1 (tail-length-report.md, box 50σ, C:12000 O:4000 H:12000 M:400, the best of three compositions by amphiphile yield) Kc(old)=mean-1=1.086226; for the target mean=15 (midpoint of 12-18) energyKT(new)=6.0+kT*ln[(15-1)/1.086226]=6.0+1.1*ln(12.8896)=8.812≈8.8 kT, and floryPrediction(8.8,1.1,c,N) with this c (the same one, calibrated once on the old data) does indeed give a predicted mean of ≈14.85, as it should. Both calibration checks failed on a real 4-temperature run (box 50σ, same composition, 50000 steps per point, kT=0.8/1.1/1.5/1.8, seed=19; data and analysis in the report): (1) the measured length distribution of separate carbon chains at kT=1.1 and energyKT=8.8 gave a mean of 2.826 (64.1% are unreacted single atoms) against Flory's predicted 14.85, a discrepancy of almost an order of magnitude, not "noise"; (2) the van 't Hoff slope of ln[p/(1-p)] against 1/kT from the measured ccBondFraction recovered 1.31 kT (r²=0.617) instead of the 8.8 kT put in, a ratio of almost 7x, and the regression is not even a straight line. The cause is not an error in the formula but the step budget: acceptanceProbability(break)=exp(-energyKT/kT) at 8.8 kT and kT=1.1 gives exp(-8)≈0.000335; the expected number of successful break attempts per bond over 50000 steps = 50000*attemptRate*dt*0.000335 ≈ 0.0084, that is, fewer than 1% of bonds get even a single chance to break during the whole run at the given attemptRate=0.05/dt=0.01. The system does not reach true thermodynamic equilibrium at any budget allowed by this task (45000-80000 steps); the measured distribution reflects the encounter/diffusion kinetics of chain growth, not Flory equilibrium. An independent regression confirms the same thing (tests/soup-bonds.test.ts's 'fewer bonds at high temperature than at low'): at this energy the test failed (at kT=1.8 there were more bonds than at kT=0.9, the reverse of the order that correct thermodynamics gives) even over 80000 steps. Outcome: the calibration is rolled back to the original 6/8 kT; in practice nothing changed, energyKT stays 6.0. The checking infrastructure (soup/src/equilibrium.ts: floryPrediction/vanHoffSlope/carbonChainLengths/ccBondFraction, tested and correct) is kept for a future attempt, which must first raise attemptRate/the step budget (attemptRate is explicitly declared as not calculated, rank D, see this file; only the forward/backward ratio is calibrated by energy) before raising energyKT any further.

Correct law (task 'kinetic-growth', 2026-08-17, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/kinetic-growth-report.md): a real covalent C-C bond does not dissociate at 175°C on any reachable timescale; the previous attempt failed precisely because it tried to describe chemistry that is genuinely irreversible with Flory's equilibrium model. Chain length here is not an equilibrium property; it is set by kinetics, by the competition between growth (this rule, catalysis-dependent) and termination (co_bond, a head at the chain end), the Fischer-Tropsch mechanism (McCollom, Ritter & Simoneit 1999, already in the project specification), whose signature is the Anderson-Schulz-Flory (ASF) distribution, N_n∝(1-α)·α^(n-1), α=k_p/(k_p+k_t). cc_break's attemptRate is now 0 (see cc_break's basis): the bond is irreversible. attemptRate=0.05 here remains k_p (the propagation attempt rate), unchanged ('growth stays catalysis-dependent, as it was'); the required co_bond.attemptRate is derived from the ratio of k_p to co_bond's k_t, see co_bond's basis. energyKT=6.0 is kept equal to cc_break's only for the sake of the assertRulesConsistent pairing invariant (detailed balance is formally defined) and as a historical record; it no longer determines the real dynamics: acceptanceProbability(break) is never evaluated, because attemptProbability(break)=0*dt=0 kills the attempt before the energy ever comes into it.

Error mechanism fixed (task 'surface-growth', 2026-08-17, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/surface-growth-report.md, diagnosis in kinetic-growth-report.md): kinetic-growth measured a systematic shortfall of the recovered α against the configured one (0.86-0.87 versus 0.933) and ~53% of carbon in chains of length 1. The cause is not this rate (k_p=0.05 did not change) but an asymmetry of the gates: cc_bond already required a catalyst (requiresCatalyst=true), whereas co_bond (termination) could fire on any carbon in the bulk; that is, propagation was catalysis-throttled while termination ran at the full nominal rate, and the configured ratio k_p/(k_p+k_t) was not the ratio the system actually saw. In real Fischer-Tropsch the growing chain stays adsorbed on its catalytic centre, and both growth and termination happen at that same centre; the chain does not wander through the solution in search of a head. The fix (soup/wgsl/bond.wgsl, propagateOnCenter/terminateOnCenter, full analysis in the file): one new buffer, centerLink, with one slot per particle and the same compareExchange pattern as bondSlots, but between species (catalyst↔growing chain end), not within one species. The catalyst holds the id of the end carbon it is currently growing (or BOND_NONE, free); the end carbon holds the id of its catalyst (or BOND_NONE if it is an unreacted monomer, or the permanently inert far end of an already started chain, or the chain has already been completed and the centre released). Propagation (roleI==roleJ==0, both carbons): nucleation (both monomers bare) requires a free catalyst nearby (the same compareExchange simultaneously checks that it is free and claims it); elongation (one bare, the other an already attached end) requires that it be specifically the owning catalyst that is physically nearby (a distance check to its own position, not the generic 'catalystNear'); merging two already started chains is deliberately forbidden (reassigning ownership of the whole chain would require an O(chain length) traversal, which this local per-pair shader does not do; growth by monomer insertion rather than by joining radicals is also physically more correct). Termination (co_bond) is now also gated through terminateOnCenter: a head can cap a chain end only if that end has an owning catalyst and that catalyst is physically nearby; an unreacted or unattached carbon can no longer be capped before it has grown as far as a centre (this was the cause of the inflated fraction of single beads). The rates k_p=cc_bond.attemptRate=0.05 and k_t=co_bond.attemptRate=0.05/14 are not changed: the derivation in co_bond's basis (α=k_p/(k_p+k_t) given an equal opportunity frequency for both event types) was arithmetically correct, it is just that previously the opportunity frequency was not equal (termination everywhere, growth only at a catalyst); now both are gated by one and the same centre availability, so it is exactly this same formula, and not a different one, that has become realisable.

Measured trap in the fix itself (surface-growth-report.md): the first version of the 'catalyst physically nearby' check in propagateOnCenter/terminateOnCenter (soup/wgsl/bond.wgsl) used the same narrow contact distance wca_cut(...) as the one-off catalyst detection at nucleation, and this stopped growth completely (measure: mean chain length 1.04, 0% amphiphiles over 60000 steps, both seeds): the catalyst and the growing end are not joined by a real bond (that would use up a valence slot from bondSlots and break the degree count in findAmphiphiles), so nothing holds them at contact distance for longer than a few steps of thermal wandering. The fix is not new physics but the correct radius of an interaction that already exists: catalyst and carbon are both polar:false, so the non-covalent Cooke-Deserno attraction (soup/wgsl/step.wgsl's nonbondedSoup, attr_dv) already acts between them out to the distance wca_cut(...)+P.wc (data/params.json's attraction.wc=1.6), not only within the contact radius; the 'catalyst still holds' check is matched against this same radius, the same attraction.wc that already regulates amphiphile assembly everywhere in this file, without a single new number.

Adsorption as a force, deadlock closed (task 'adsorption', 2026-08-17, adsorption-report.md): the previous paragraph ('Error mechanism fixed') made the right diagnosis but treated only the symptom (the check radius), not the cause itself: 'nothing holds them at contact distance for longer than a few steps of thermal wandering' described the real state of affairs quite correctly, but the conclusion from it should have been 'so a force is needed', not 'let us widen the check radius'. The widened radius (this entry) reduced the problem (max chain length 5→9-10) but did not close it (recovered α 0.36-0.40 versus 0.9333, 0 amphiphiles); see surface-growth-report.md §3-4 in full. The fix in task 'adsorption': the catalyst<->tip bond now carries a real FENE spring (see data/soup.json's adsorption and soup/wgsl/step.wgsl's bondedForce) through a separate buffer (centerLink), not bondSlots; valence and findAmphiphiles are untouched, exactly as in the previous entry. The measured before/after numbers (single-bead fraction, recovered vs configured α, desorption/termination counts, free-centre fraction, tail length, aggregate shapes) are in adsorption-report.md.

Disabled, irreversible (task 'kinetic-growth', 2026-08-17, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/kinetic-growth-report.md): attemptRate set to zero. The break rule is kept in the file (as the task required, 'so that the history stays readable'; it is also needed for the assertRulesConsistent invariant: cc_bond must have a paired break with the same energyKT), but it never fires: attemptProbability(r,dt)=attemptRate*dt=0*dt=0 for any dt, so acceptanceProbability (the one formula that carries detailed balance) is never even computed for this bond in a real run. Justification for the change of law: the covalent C-C bond does not dissociate at 175°C on any reachable laboratory or model time scale (real Fischer-Tropsch chemistry, McCollom/Ritter/Simoneit 1999, two to three days at 175°C, distribution C2 to C35+, already cited in the project specification, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-protocell-genesis-design.md). Chain length in this chemistry is not an equilibrium property (a reversible bond with fast breaking); it is set kinetically by the competition between growth and termination on the catalytic surface. The signature of the mechanism is the geometric Anderson-Schulz-Flory (ASF) distribution, N_n∝(1-α)·α^(n-1), whose single parameter is the propagation probability α=k_p/(k_p+k_t). The previous attempt (energy-calibration-report.md) kept cc_break enabled and tried to imitate long chains through an equilibrium energy (8.8 kT). Both checks (comparison with Flory, the van 't Hoff slope) failed precisely because the real kinetics of this model is already irreversible on the reachable step budget at such a depth (accept(break)≈0.000335, <1% of bonds get even one chance to break in 50000 steps). In other words, the system was already behaving as irreversible; it simply had not been honestly declared as such. This switch does the same thing explicitly, on a physical justification, rather than as a side effect of an overly deep energy. Rank D: a modelling decision (not a measured C-C dissociation rate constant, which at 175°C in practice simply does not exist), whose consequence is checked not by van 't Hoff (no longer applicable: there is no equilibrium that a slope could recover) but by agreement of the measured C-C chain length distribution with the ASF prediction at the configured α, without fitting; see kinetic-growth-report.md. attemptRate=0 (rather than removing the rule or adding a separate boolean flag) was chosen as the minimal, least invasive way to disable it: it needs no edits to soup/src/rules.ts, soup/src/sim.ts or soup/wgsl/bond.wgsl, because attemptProbability already multiplies by attemptRate, so the 0 propagates to attemptProbForm/attemptProbBreak automatically through the existing path packVec4(rules.map(...attemptProbability...)) in soup/src/sim.ts, with no new code.

estimate: attachment of a polar head to the chain end, deeper than the C-C bond, so the head does not drop off first.

RATE derived (task 'kinetic-growth', 2026-08-17, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/kinetic-growth-report.md): attemptRate lowered from 0.05 to 0.0035714286 to set the propagation:termination proportion (ASF α); the binding location (chain end only, terminalOnly), catalysis independence and energyKT=8.0 are untouched, per the task. Both rules (cc_bond and co_bond) are bond formation events, for which acceptanceProbability(bond)=min(1,exp(+energyKT/kT))=1 always (energy enters acceptance only for a break, see rules.ts's acceptanceProbability); that is, the relative frequency with which propagation beats termination in the competition for one and the same growing chain end is directly the ratio of their attemptRate values, with no separate geometric calibration (unlike the rolled-back energy-calibration attempt, where 'c' was needed only because it compared the break of an already existing bond with an equilibrium encounter model; here both sides of the competition are the same type of event, formation, evaluated in one and the same neighbour walk of bond_form_main). Arithmetic: the target is a mean tail length in the real range of membrane lipids (12-18 atoms, midpoint 15). For a geometric (ASF) distribution mean=1/(1-α) ⇒ α=(mean-1)/mean=14/15≈0.933333. Branching ratio k_p/(k_p+k_t)=α ⇒ k_t/k_p=(1-α)/α=(1/15)/(14/15)=1/14. k_p=cc_bond.attemptRate=0.05 (unchanged). k_t=co_bond.attemptRate=k_p/14=0.05/14=0.00357142857142857...≈0.0035714286. A check without fitting: comparison of the measured length distribution of C-C chains (soup/src/equilibrium.ts's carbonChainLengths, the same C-C-only population that floryPrediction already used; heads do not merge it) with asfPrediction(14/15, N), see the report. Known risk, recorded in advance (not after the fact): with co_bond 14x slower than the old value, the fraction of carbon that manages to get a head within the same step budget (45000-60000) drops, by a rough linear estimate, from the measured ~31% (old co_bond=0.05, tail-length-report.md) to ~2%; that is, most chains at the checkpoint are still actively growing and have not completed termination, so the measured distribution may reflect the current state of growth rather than a settled ASF ensemble. This is not a reason to raise k_p together with k_t (which would violate 'growth stays catalysis-dependent, as it was' and would go beyond the Poisson-thinning regime bondAttemptInterval.steps=20 already validated at attemptRate=0.05, perf-report.md); it is an explicitly predicted, honestly measured limitation, analysed in kinetic-growth-report.md.

requiresCatalyst kept false (task 'surface-growth', 2026-08-17, surface-growth-report.md): kinetic-growth diagnosed that termination could fire on any carbon in the bulk, not only at a catalyst. The fix is not through this flag (requiresCatalyst=true would check 'a catalyst somewhere near particle i of the dispatch thread', and for co_bond i is the lower-indexed member of the carbon/head pair, so in half of the cases the check would be made around the head rather than around the end carbon, the wrong distance) but through a new function, soup/wgsl/bond.wgsl's terminateOnCenter: termination is now allowed only when the carbon being capped has its own owning catalyst (centerLink, set exactly at nucleation/elongation of that same chain by cc_bond) and that catalyst is physically nearby (a direct distance check to its own position, the same wca_cut that catalystNear uses). attemptRate=0.0035714286 and energyKT=8.0 were not changed: the k_p:k_t proportion itself remains correct (see cc_bond's basis, section 'Error mechanism fixed'); it is just that its implementation was dishonest because termination was left ungated; now both events are gated by one and the same centre availability.

Rate recalculated for the surface population, not for the bulk (task 'rate-rederivation', 2026-08-17, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/rate-rederivation-report.md, diagnosis in adsorption-report.md §7): adsorption-report.md measured that even after both events (propagation and termination) came to be gated by one and the same centre availability, co_bond actually fires ~700-800 times less often than cc_bond (5-6 versus 3940/3812 events over 60000 steps, both seeds), whereas the configured ratio k_p:k_t=14:1 implies only 14x. The cause, named but not recalculated in adsorption-report.md: the k_p:k_t ratio is realised literally only if the candidate detection frequency (the geometric encounter in bondFormWalk, before the attemptProb roll) is the same for both sides of the competition, and it is not the same, because 'how many carbons are able to extend the chain at the centre' and 'how many heads are able to reach the held end' are populations that differ in size and in local density: bare carbons (free valence) make up practically all of the bulk C (12000, composition C:O=3:1), and, on top of that, the catalyst (M, non-polar) non-covalently attracts carbon by the same Cooke-Deserno formula (soup/wgsl/step.wgsl's nonbondedSoup) that the polar head O is not subject to (a head/non-polar pair is not attracted); that is, carbons are locally enriched at the centre above the bulk composition, while heads stay at bulk density. A direct analytical count of the populations (bulk composition 3:1, difference between the C-C/C-O WCA contact radii ~1.09x) gives a correction of only ×3-4, which is not enough; a purely theoretical count of 'how many centres are occupied' (12000/~390 active tips ≈30x, the predecessor's own estimate) is not enough either, because after this same fix (adsorption) propagation and termination run on one and the same set of active tips, not on sets of centres of different size, so the count of centres from both sides cancels out in the ratio rather than entering it. The correct multiplier is the ratio of the geometric detection frequency of each candidate type at an active tip, not of candidate populations in general, and it is measured, not calculated on paper, precisely because it includes the emergent enrichment above, occupancy=1 and re-adsorption, all of which are already inside the measured events.

Recalculation from the model, not a guess: attemptProbability(rule,dt)=attemptRate*dt (soup/src/rules.ts) with batching bondAttemptInterval.steps=20 (data/soup.json) gives the probability of success of one already detected candidate per dispatch cycle: attemptProb_prop=kProp*dt*20=0.05*0.01*20=0.01 (propagation), attemptProb_term(old)=kTerm*dt*20=(0.05/14)*0.01*20=0.01/14≈0.00071429 (termination). Acceptance (acceptanceProbability) for bond formation is always 1 (rules.ts), so each candidate detection is an independent Bernoulli trial with this probability; hence the number of geometric detections (opportunity) over the whole run is recovered exactly from the measured number of successful events by dividing by attemptProb, a quantity that does not depend on the rate itself (it is set by diffusion/geometry, not by Metropolis), so this operation gives the true count of 'candidates able to reach' on both sides, without circularly reusing the very number we are trying to correct. From the final run of adsorption-report.md (§9, run 5/5, box 50σ, C:12000 O:4000 H:12000 M:400, kT=1.1, 60000 steps, seeds 19 and 23, the same code, which this task does not touch): summed over the two seeds, ccBondEvents=3940+3812=7752, coBondEvents=5+6=11. opportunity_prop=7752/0.01=775200; opportunity_term=11/(0.01/14)=11*1400=15400. solvent.basis:
task 'explicit-water' (2026-08-18, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/explicit-water-report.md). Motivation: .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/periodic-measurement-report.md §4: two independent methods (one of which never unwraps coordinates) agreed that the interior of the largest aggregate of this campaign is empty (24.9-34.6 σ³ against a threshold of 370.8656 σ³); with an implicit solvent the interior of a vesicle would be a vacuum, which is energetically unfavourable for anything and ought to be displaced by filling. Explicit water makes the hydrophobic effect emergent: tails are avoided by water rather than attracted to each other by a given rule.

1. Water bead definition (rank D). One bead on the same bead scale as the other monomers of this file (radiusSigma=1.0, the same scale as the tail C), by the direct requirement of the task "at the same bead scale as the existing monomers", not a free size parameter. How many real water molecules this represents: this project has no real σ→nm conversion, but there are two numbers already measured in this tree that were themselves calibrated against the Cooke&Deserno literature and therefore give an independent anchor for an estimate: the measured area per lipid a=1.2089σ² (verify/out/gates.json, gate area-per-lipid) and the measured thickness t=4.457σ (same gate, bilayer-thickness). (a) via area: taking a real phospholipid area per lipid of ~0.65 nm² (a typical order for DPPC/POPC, a rough literature anchor, not a gate of this project), σ=sqrt(0.65/1.2089)≈0.734 nm; the volume of one bead as a close-packed sphere of diameter σ: (4/3)π(σ/2)³≈0.207 nm³; the volume of one water molecule 18.015 g/mol / (0.997 g/cm³ · 6.022e23) ≈ 0.0300 nm³; ratio ≈6.9. (b) via thickness: taking a real bilayer hydrophobic-core thickness of ~4 nm (rough order), σ=4/4.457≈0.897 nm; the same volume calculation (volume grows as σ³, the ratio is (0.897/0.734)³≈1.83 times larger than in (a)) gives ≈12.6. Both estimates are rough orders of magnitude with different assumptions (sphere packing, a borrowed literature area/thickness rather than our own), so a range of ≈7-13 is taken, rounded to "about ten real water molecules per CG bead", not a single pseudo-precise number. polar=false (water does not carry the charge of the carboxyl group, it is not a head), solvent=true, a new flag that distinguishes water from the inert neutral C/H/M.

2. Interaction scheme. WCA stays on every pair without exception (soup/wgsl/step.wgsl's nonbondedSoup, untouched). Attraction (Cooke-Deserno attr_dv, the same P.epsilon/P.wc as before; these rank A parameters from data/params.json are not touched, because the Cooke&Deserno calibration concerns the shape and depth of the attraction well, not which pairs receive it): water-water and water-head attract (this is exactly hydrophilicity: water 'likes' itself and the polar head group), water-tail does not attract (the displacement is exactly the hydrophobic effect, emergently), head-head does not attract (unchanged: heads did not attract each other before either, they are polar, and the old rule !polar&&!polar already excluded them).

3. The old tail-tail term: removed entirely, not reduced. The old rule (!speciesPolar(ti)&&!speciesPolar(tj) → attraction) made any pair of non-polar particles attract: not only tail-tail, but also tail-catalyst, tail-donor, catalyst-catalyst and so on. It was a manual substitute for the hydrophobic effect (the project's assignment calls it exactly that). Keeping it switched on alongside the water-tail exclusion would mean counting the same physics twice: the explicit repulsion of the tail from water already gives the tails a motive to gather together (where there is no water, there is another tail), and the old term would add one more direct attractive force on top; the effective depth of the tail-tail interaction would end up roughly twice what the explicit-solvent model implies. Decision (not silently keeping both): remove the old term completely rather than halving it or cutting it by an arbitrary fraction. Cutting it by 'some amount' would be a new uncalculated number without justification (forbidden by the same 'no numeric constants' rule), whereas zero is the only value that needs no fitting. Implementation: the rewritten attraction condition (solvent_i&&solvent_j)||(solvent_i&&polar_j)||(polar_i&&solvent_j) structurally never includes a (non-polar,non-polar) pair without water in any case; the zero comes from the form of the rule itself, not from a separate 'if tail-tail, set to zero'. A side effect that has to be stated honestly: the catalyst (M) and the donor (H), which are also non-polar, used to receive this attraction too (surface-growth-report.md explicitly documents that the catalyst<->carbon attraction helped association before the real FENE adsorption spring appeared); now they lose it as well. The catalytic mechanism (the requiresCatalyst gate, the centerLink tether) is untouched in code, but the actual nucleation rate may slow down, because a free catalyst now approaches free carbon only by diffusion+WCA contact, without the auxiliary attraction; see the report for the measurement.

4. Calibration. Explicit water is a different model from the one on which the area-per-lipid/bilayer-thickness corridor was measured (Cooke&Deserno 2005: implicit solvent, tail-tail attraction as a manual ersatz). The water radiusSigma=1.0 was chosen by the task's requirement ('the same bead scale'), not fitted in advance. The result of the measurement of a bilayer patch in water (the area-per-lipid/thickness numbers, and whether or not they fell into the corridor [1.1,1.5]σ²/[4,6]σ) and any calibration attempt (if one was needed): see explicit-water-report.md, the section on revalidation. If the corridor is not reached within this task's budget, the report says so directly rather than staying silent.
