task 'acid-soap-pairing' (2026-08-23, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/acid-soap-pairing-report.md; read it in full, this is the summary).

1. What this is. The only attraction in the model that reads not two species but a dynamic variable: it acts between one protonated head (q=0, neutral carboxylic acid) and one deprotonated head (q=-1, carboxylate), that is, between an acid and a soap, and between nothing else. That is why this is not a pairEpsilon cell (its key is a pair of classes, its value is a property of the species): the polarPolar cell would attract both acid-acid and soap-soap, and the atomistic measurement in §2 says this does not happen in water. The rule lives in three places that must agree: soup/wgsl/pair.wgsl's acidSoapScale() (force), soup/src/electrostatics.ts's pairingStats (population) and soup/src/acid-soap.ts (pair identity and its lifetime). The protonation state is taken from chargeRO, whose only writer is the constant-pH MC; no new state and no new species were added.

2. Where the number comes from. The atomistic engine of this repository (atomic/, MACE-OFF23) measured the association of two carboxyl heads, comparing states of identical composition. Neutral acid+acid: 16.43 kcal/mol in vacuum and −5.51 kcal/mol with 32 waters (so in water the neutral dimer is unfavourable: the competition of water for hydrogen bonds wins; this is the known fact that carboxylic acids dimerise in the gas phase and in non-polar solvents, but not in water). Acid+carboxylate (a real acid-soap pair, system charge −1): 21.04 kcal/mol in vacuum and +10.38 kcal/mol with 32 waters, and all four independent starting geometries converged to one minimum. This very contrast is the mechanism of the pH window of fatty-acid vesicles, and before this task it was structurally impossible in the coarse-grained model: polarPolar was exactly 0.0 throughout the project's history.

3. The mapping, explicitly. 10.38 kcal/mol = 43.4299 kJ/mol. It is normalised in the same way as every pairEpsilon level: divided by reference (apolarApolar, 3.5 kJ/mol, MARTINI 2.1) → 12.4086 in the dimensionless units of the table, that is, 12.4 times deeper than the reference apolar pair. The well shape (onset rc=wca_cut(sigma*b_tt), width wc, depth epsilon) is attr_dv's own, rank A, untouched; only the multiplier is taken from here.

4. Why 12.4086 is an upper bound, not a value. What was measured is the energy, not the free energy. The entropic cost of pairing was not computed (it needs enhanced sampling, which the atomistic engine does not have), and it works against the pair: two molecules that have lost rotational and translational degrees of freedom pay for it. In addition, a coarse-grained bead is not an atom: transferring the absolute depth from an all-atom calculation into the energy unit of this model would be fitting of the same kind that §4 of the attractionScale.basis field forbids for MARTINI. Therefore 12.4086 is taken as a ceiling, and the strength is swept.

5. The sweep and what it measured (charged bilayer patch in explicit water 0.8 sigma^-3, 400 lipids, pH 7.0, MC area move at zero tension, tests/soup-acid-soap-bilayer.test.ts, artefact verify/out/acid-soap-strength-sweep.json). Strength (fraction of the ceiling) → area [corridor 1.1-1.5] / thickness [corridor 4-6] / alpha / paired fraction / pair lifetime:
  S=0 (0.000) → 1.2026 [1.1979,1.2071] inside / 4.4191 inside / alpha 0.9446 / 0.0917 / 2686 steps; passed
  S=1 (0.081) → 1.1556 [1.1510,1.1593] inside / 4.5080 inside / alpha 0.6808 / 0.3587 / 2857 steps; passed
  S=2 (0.161) → 1.1510 [1.1473,1.1546] inside / 4.5517 inside / alpha 0.5921 / 0.4246 / 2947 steps; passed
  S=4 (0.322) → 1.1042 [1.0972,1.1149] outside (below 1.1) / 4.9729 inside / alpha 0.5396 / 0.4088 / 5690; failed
  S=8 (0.645) → 1.2154 inside / 1.4191 outside / alpha 0.5100 / 0.3438 / 11250; failed, the area did not settle
  S=12.409 (1.000, ceiling) → 1.1637 inside / 1.0079 outside / alpha 0.5017 / 0.3079 / 17285; failed, did not settle
So the measured ceiling destroys the bilayer: at S>=8 the thickness drops to 1.0-1.4 sigma against the corridor of 4-6. Chosen: epsilonKJ = 7.0 kJ/mol = S 2.0 = 0.161 of the ceiling = 1.67 kcal/mol, the largest swept depth at which both literature corridors hold on a settled area (ln A drift, t=0.70), and it also gives the largest paired fraction (0.4246) and the largest excess of unlike contacts (1.154). No corridor was widened, no rank A constant was refitted, co_bond.attemptRate is untouched.

6. Rank D, and this is said plainly. The ceiling 12.4086 is rank B (computed, not measured: MACE-OFF23 is an ML potential, and this is energy without entropy). The value used is a fraction of that ceiling chosen by a sweep against this tree's own gates, that is, an estimate, rank D. By the project rule (specification, section 3), gates that rest only on D come out unproven by definition, and any gates that are built on this number must carry this rank. Claiming rank A or B here would mean passing off energy as free energy.

7. Feedback into titration is not optional. Changing the protonation state of a head changes whom it pairs with, so the pair term enters the same dG as the screened Coulomb term, in the constant-pH MC (soup/src/acid-soap.ts's acidSoapSiteWork, called from protonationSweep). Without this the sampling would follow a distribution inconsistent with the potential that the dynamics integrates: the same class of silent inconsistency as a stale F(x). And this is also the mechanism itself: a head among charged neighbours gains the pair energy by becoming neutral, and vice versa, so the pair term is a restoring force on alpha towards 1/2. Measured: at pH 7.0 alpha goes 0.9446 (S=0) → 0.6808 (S=1) → 0.5921 (S=2) → 0.5017 (S=12.409); at pH 4 alpha goes 0.1122 (S=0) → 0.2556 (S=2), that is, towards 1/2 from both sides. The exact Boltzmann weights of a two-head system are pinned together with this term in tests/soup-electrostatics.test.ts.

8. What this did not do, stated right here. Closure did not become the cheapest edge-free object at any swept strength: the band [closure floor, spherical micelle] is inverted by a factor of 46.8-53.2 against the previous 44-58, L* shifted 160.6-161.3 → 155.1-159.3 sigma (tests/soup-acid-soap-arithmetic.test.ts). The packing parameter p=v/(a0*lc) in this model is identically 1 by construction and is not an independent argument.

attractionScale.basis:
task 'hydrophobic-asymmetry' (2026-08-19, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/hydrophobic-asymmetry-report.md; read it in full, this is the summary).

1. This is an explicit reversal of §3 of the solvent.basis field above ("The old tail-tail term: removed entirely"). The requirement of task 'explicit-water' ("no tail-tail attraction, hydrophobicity must be emergent") was revoked by the project owner as wrong as physics, and here is why: real hydrocarbon chains attract each other through London dispersion, and in explicit-solvent coarse-grained models this term is present. The argument of §3 ("double counting: the explicit displacement by water already gives the tails a motive to gather") did not survive checking. There is no displacement as a separate force in the model: water-tail was not repelled in any version beyond the general WCA, so removing the tail-tail term did not remove a duplicate; it removed the only force of lateral cohesion of the leaflet. Measurement of this consequence: headBuriedFraction 0.40-0.49 (almost half of the heads sit inside the hydrophobic zone, whole lipids have passed through the sheet) with a dry core; see water-calibration-report.md §1. Hydrophobicity stays emergent, but its mechanism is a ratio of depths, not the absence of a term: segregation follows the sign of the exchange energy eps_ww + eps_tt - 2*eps_wt (in Flory-Huggins this is chi), which here is positive and larger than it was without tail-tail.

2. Where the ratios come from (rank C: independent literature, not calibrated on this tree). MARTINI (Marrink et al. 2007, J. Phys. Chem. B 111:7812), taken neither from memory nor from a retelling, but from the parameter file itself, martini_v2.1.itp, section [nonbond_params] (official cgmartini library: https://cgmartini-library.s3.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/1_Downloads/ff_parameters/martini2/particle-definitions/martini_v2.1.itp). The level legend comes from the same file: O 'supra attractive' eps=5.6; I 'attractive' 5.0; II 'almost attractive' 4.5; III 'semi attractive' 4.0; IV 'intermediate' 3.5; ... VIII 'repulsive' 2.0 (s=0.47 nm throughout). The pairs taken and the recalculation eps=C6^2/(4*C12) from the file's own lines are in pairEpsilon.levels[*].martini, next to each number. Mapping of this model's classes onto MARTINI types: tail carbon C → C1 (alkane); water W → P4 (this is exactly martini water); head O is uncharged polar (this model has no electrostatics at all, see saltPhLimitation), so it corresponds to the uncharged polar lipid bead Na (the glycerol-ester bead of DPPC), and not to the charged Qa of a carboxylate: hence solventPolar = P4-Na = 4.0. An alternative mapping of the head onto P1 would give 4.5, i.e. the ratio solventPolar/apolarApolar would change from 1.143 to 1.286 (+12%); this is a recorded uncertainty of the choice, not a hidden one.

3. An important correction to the previous report. water-calibration-report.md §2 (and the former text of this field) claimed that water-water is level I (5.0) and non-polar/non-polar is "often level O" (5.6), i.e. that apolar-apolar is the strongest level. According to the parameter file this is wrong: C1-C1 = level IV 'intermediate' (3.5), and P4-P4 = level I (5.0). So water-water is 1.43 times stronger than tail-tail, not weaker. Hydrophobicity does not suffer from this: it rests not on "the strongest level for the non-polar ones" but on the exchange energy 5.0 + 3.5 - 2*2.0 = +4.5 kJ/mol > 0 (demixing). The numbers are corrected here, not fitted to the earlier wording.

4. The absolute scale is not refitted. reference='apolarApolar': the ratios are normalised to the tail-tail pair, and its multiplier is exactly 1.0, so the tail-tail well depth in the soup is again equal to epsilon from data/params.json (rank A, Cooke & Deserno 2005), bit for bit the same as on the solvent-free path, which is calibrated and passes the gate (area 1.2046σ², thickness 4.5126σ). Only the ratios (dimensionless) are taken from MARTINI; not a single kJ/mol is converted into the energy unit of this model: MARTINI has its own temperature and its own bead scale, and transferring absolute depths would be fitting. epsilonScale=1.0 (rank D) is kept as a single common multiplier of the whole table (and as the entry point for CreateSoupOpts.solventAttractionScaleOverride in sweeps); it has not changed.

5. Side effects, stated plainly. (a) By construction (a class, not an id), apolar-apolar restores attraction not only to the tail-tail pair but also to pairs with the catalyst M and the donor H, the very ones that lost it with the removal in 'explicit-water' (see §3 of solvent.basis and surface-growth-report.md: the catalyst<->carbon attraction helped association). This is physically consistent (M and H are non-polar here, and London dispersion does not know that a bead has been assigned as a catalyst) and also restores the earlier nucleation kinetics; the dynamics of the soup changes because of it, the changes were measured before/after in the task report, and the tests were not fitted to them. (b) A weak water-tail term (0.571) has appeared: the previous report said that no literature grounds for a water-tail attraction had been found; the MARTINI file shows the opposite: P4-C1 is a 2.0 kJ/mol well labelled 'repulsive' (the label refers to the level on the scale, not to the sign of the force). It weakens segregation, but the exchange energy still stays positive, see §1.

areaMove.basis:
task 'hydrophobic-asymmetry' (2026-08-19), defect 2: the area per lipid must be measured at zero tension rather than assumed equal to the middle of the corridor at a fixed box. The mechanism is the same as in engine/src/sim-area-move.ts (an MC area move with a configurational Jacobian and rigid translation of molecules by their centre of mass), carried over to the soup path (soup/src/soup-area-move.ts) rather than a second copy of it: the coordinate map is the already existing scaleMoleculesRigid (soup/src/soup-box-scale-math.ts, itself a generalisation of scaleLateralRigid), and applying it to the GPU state is the already existing applyBoxScaleOnce.

logDelta (the half-width of the proposal u ~ U(-logDelta,+logDelta) in ln area) is a setting of the step size of the Markov chain, not a physical parameter: it does not affect the equilibrium distribution, only how fast it is explored. The value is taken the same as already measured in engine/src/sim-area-move.ts (acceptance fraction 0.54/0.36/0.23 at half-widths 0.006/0.010/0.016, so 0.012 falls within the working range 0.2-0.6); it lives here rather than in the code because params.test.ts forbids numeric model constants in soup/src.

mode='lateral-fixed-volume' means the move changes the area at constant volume: Lx,Ly ×sqrt(s), Lz ÷s. This is a forced choice, not a matter of taste, and here is the measurable reason. The engine variant (Lx,Ly ×sqrt(s), Lz fixed) in an implicit solvent imposes the condition "lateral pressure = 0", which for a membrane in vacuum coincides with "tension = 0". With explicit water this no longer holds: the water fills the box, and at fixed Lz a change of area changes the volume, so the equilibrium of such a move is set by the absolute pressure of the water (its equation of state at 0.8σ⁻³) rather than by the membrane tension; the area per lipid would come out as a consequence of the solvent's compressibility. A move at constant volume imposes P_lat = P_norm, that is, exactly gamma=0, and does not require knowing the absolute pressure of the water.

Jacobian. The general form of the acceptance: min(1, exp(-(dU - Nmol*kT*ln(V'/V))/kT)), Nmol = the number of independent molecules (connected components of the covalent graph; each free water bead is a component of size 1, and water enters Nmol on a par with the lipids). With Lz fixed, V'/V = A'/A, and the formula coincides with engine/src/sim-area-move.ts: N*kT*ln(A'/A). At constant volume ln(V'/V)=0 and the entropic term vanishes identically; this is not a dropped term but the same term evaluated at that point. Physically: the ideal-gas part of the pressure is isotropic and does no work on a volume-preserving deformation. Both branches are checked by measuring the identity <dU/dlnA>_bead - <dU/dlnA>_CM = (Nbeads - Nmolecules)*kT (a generalisation of the 2NkT check from the engine); the numbers are in the task report.

electrostatics.basis:
task 'electrostatics' (2026-08-20, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/electrostatics-report.md; read it in full). Why. The predecessor ('final-campaign', same directory) named as the binding constraint "(3) connectivity: the stock percolates": with the two-tailed composition the organic phase wrapped along 3 of 3 axes at every wet checkpoint (r_g 26.25–27.19 against 27.000 for a uniformly filled box 54), that is, the object had no interior region that could be closed. Neutral heads predict exactly this: nothing sets the effective head area, so nothing stops aggregates from stitching together. Real fatty acids are acids: the head sits in a protonation equilibrium (COOH ⇄ COO⁻ + H⁺), the deprotonated one carries −e, like heads repel, and this repulsion is precisely what sets a0 in the Israelachvili packing parameter p = v/(a0·l_c). The literature window for fatty-acid vesicles (pH ≈ 7–9; the apparent pKa falls by ~0.7 as NaCl rises from 10 to 100 mM; design.md, "Gate 5", PMC7575682) exists precisely because of this equilibrium: above it, micelles; below it, oil/crystal. The field saltPhLimitation.represented has been switched to true for exactly the part that is now represented, and the same place lists what remains unrepresented.

1. Interaction form, rank B: Debye–Hückel / screened Coulomb, U(r) = kT·(l_B/σ)·q_i·q_j·exp(−r/λ_D)/r. This is the standard coarse-grained way to account for an electrolyte when the ions are not explicit (Debye & Hückel, Phys. Z. 24 (1923) 185; Israelachvili, "Intermolecular and Surface Forces", 3rd ed., ch. 14; in CG practice, the MARTINI screened Coulomb with a cutoff of ~1.2 nm, Marrink et al., J. Phys. Chem. B 111 (2007) 7812). The cutoff is a shifted force, not a bare truncation: F_sf(r) = F(r) − F(rc), U_sf(r) = U(r) − U(rc) + (r−rc)·F(rc) (Toxvaerd & Dyre, J. Chem. Phys. 134 (2011) 081102; Allen & Tildesley, 2nd ed., §5.2). The reason is not cosmetic: every other term of this engine is continuous at its own cutoff (WCA goes to zero at 2^(1/6)·b, the cos² ramp of attr_dv at rc+wc); a bare Coulomb truncation would be the only discontinuous force in the model and would break the agreement between the CPU potential and the GPU force that tests/soup-area-move.test.ts pins. The cutoff of this term is its own, long, and not shared with Lennard-Jones (task 'long-range-electrostatics', 2026-08-20, see item 12): Coulomb, even screened, is physically longer-ranged than the WCA core, and the first version of this section took rc = wca_cut(b_tt)+wc = 2.7224620 σ for the sake of "not a single new number", which at 10 mM cut off 84 % of the integrated interaction and gave a salt-induced pKa shift of −0.124 against the literature's ~0.7. Now rc_es = longRangeDebyeLengths·λ_D, that is, a multiple of its own screening length, capped at longRangeMaxBoxFraction·min(box) by the minimum-image convention.

2. The σ → nm mapping is a range, and the range is carried forward, rank C. This project has no length calibration: σ is the Cooke & Deserno bead (data/params.json, rank A). Two independent estimates: (a) from the measured area per lipid of 1.1777 σ² against ~0.6–0.7 nm² for a two-tailed lipid → σ ≈ 0.71–0.77 nm; (b) from the measured bilayer thickness of 4.7990 σ against 4–5 nm → σ ≈ 0.83–1.04 nm. In total σ ∈ [0.65, 1.00] nm; the shipped value is 0.80. This is the entire uncertainty in the interaction strength, because both A = kT·l_B/σ and κ = σ/λ_D are linear in σ: A ∈ [0.781, 1.202] ε·σ, λ_D ∈ [0.961, 1.479] σ at 100 mM, and the contact repulsion of two charged heads U_sf(0.95 σ) ranges over [0.2245, 0.4234] kT, a factor of 1.886 between the ends. No calibration has been invented to narrow this range; every result in the report carries it along.

3. l_B = 0.71 nm, rank B: the Bjerrum length of water at 298 K (e²/(4πε₀ε_r k_B T) at ε_r = 78.4), the generally accepted tabulated value (Israelachvili, 3rd ed., ch. 4 and 14).

4. λ_D(1 M) = 0.304 nm, rank B, the standard Debye-length coefficient for a 1:1 electrolyte at 298 K: λ_D = 0.304 nm/√(I[M]) (Israelachvili, 3rd ed., ch. 14: 0.96 nm at 100 mM, 3.04 nm at 10 mM, exactly the two points between which the literature measures the 0.7 shift in apparent pKa).

5. I = 0.1 M by default, rank B: the upper point of the literature's own salt interval (10 → 100 mM NaCl), chosen as the shipped value because at it λ_D = 1.20 σ and the cutoff at 2.72 σ leaves exp(−2.27) = 10.4 % of the contact value behind it, whereas at 10 mM λ_D = 3.80 σ and the same cutoff cuts the interaction off at 49 % of its unscreened magnitude. This was true for the former 2.72 σ cutoff and was its main defect; with the cutoff of item 12 (a multiple of λ_D) the discarded fraction is the same in both salt arms, so the shift between 10 and 100 mM is no longer biased to one side by truncation. Overridden per run (--ionicStrength), because it is a parameter of the experiment, not a constant of the model.

6. pKa_intrinsic = 4.9, rank B: the pKa of a monomeric fatty acid in water (octanoic 4.89, decanoic 4.9; CRC Handbook, Dissociation constants of organic acids). It is deliberately the monomeric value, not the apparent interfacial one (7–9), and this matters in principle: the shift of the apparent pKa at a crowded charged surface must emerge from the dU_es of the Monte Carlo below, not be written in. The Born (self-energy) term is already absorbed into this number; there is no separate solvation term in the model.

7. Protonation is a dynamic variable, not a label, rank B for the scheme. Discrete constant-pH Monte Carlo: a randomly chosen head, an attempted state flip, Metropolis on dG(prot → deprot) = kT·ln(10)·(pKa_intrinsic − pH) + dU_es, where dU_es is the screened-Coulomb work of placing the charge into this bead's own current environment. This is the standard form of constant-pH MC / the semi-grand ensemble (Baptista, Teixeira & Soares, J. Chem. Phys. 117 (2002) 4184; Mongan & Case, Curr. Opin. Struct. Biol. 15 (2005) 157; Donnini et al., JCTC 7 (2011) 1962). Detailed balance: single-site flips, the site is chosen at random, and the forward and reverse dG at a fixed environment differ only in sign, so P(f)/P(r) = exp(−dG/kT) exactly; this is numerically pinned in tests/soup-electrostatics.test.ts against the exact Boltzmann weights of a two-head system, and it is checked separately that at zero dU_es the measured α matches Henderson–Hasselbalch.

8. sweepEverySteps = 1000, rank D, an engineering choice, not a physical rate: it is exactly the synchronisation step that the step() loop already makes (soup/src/soup-integrate.ts's STEP_CHUNK), so the sweep adds not a single extra pipeline stall. The bias, stated plainly: protonation comes out quasi-static relative to the dynamics (1000 steps = 10 τ), that is, the H⁺ equilibrium is over-equilibrated if its real relaxation is slower.

9. What is not represented, so that this does not go stale silently: no explicit H⁺, no explicit Na⁺/Cl⁻ (screening is a mean-field length, not particles), no titration of the medium (pH is an external constant of the run; a crowded surface cannot locally deplete protons), no COOH···COO⁻ hydrogen bond (the polarPolar level in this file stays 0 and is not touched by this task, so the acid-soap pair is not inserted as a species and can show up only as a charge-alternation correlation, which is what is measured), no electrostatics in the bond Metropolis (as before this task, it uses only the energyKT of its rule; it already ignored changes in WCA and attraction before), no ion condensation or charge inversion (a consequence of the mean-field screen).

10. Every bead of species O is charged, not only a head already sitting on a chain: a free O is a bare carboxyl group, and it titrates the same way. The alternative (charging only bonded heads) would mean a jump in charge at the moment of bond formation, that is, a non-equilibrium coupling of chemistry to protonation; it was rejected for this reason, not for cost.

11. enabled = false by default. With enabled=false the coefficient A is zero, the term is identically zero, and every predecessor run is bit-for-bit the same. It is switched on per run (--charge); pH and ionic strength are also run flags, because they are parameters of the experiment (like --steps), not constants of the model.

12. Long range: its own cutoff, a multiple of the Debye length, rank B on the multiple (task 'long-range-electrostatics', 2026-08-20, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/long-range-electrostatics-report.md; read it in full). Why. A screened Coulomb decays as exp(−r/λ_D)/r, so the fraction of the integrated interaction beyond the cutoff is exactly exp(−x)(1+x) at x = rc/λ_D: at the former cutoff of 2.7224620 σ this is 0.339 at 100 mM and 0.839 at 10 mM; that is, the truncation weakened most the very arm that must show the larger penalty, and the measured salt shift of the apparent pKa came out at −0.124 against the literature's ~0.7. What was chosen and why exactly this. longRangeDebyeLengths = 4: (a) at x = 4, 9.16 % of the integrated interaction and exp(−4) = 1.83 % of the contact value remain beyond the cutoff, while the contact repulsion of two heads U_sf(0.95 σ) stays within 0.8 % of its untruncated value (measured: 0.7215 kT against 0.7276 kT at 10 mM, σ = 0.80 nm); (b) there is a single multiple for all salt levels, so the discarded fraction is equal in the 10 and 100 mM arms and the salt shift is no longer biased by truncation; (c) 4·λ_D(10 mM) = 15.20 σ is the largest multiple that, at σ = 0.80 nm, still fits the minimum-image convention in both phases of the campaign with box 54 (dry box 36.637 → cap 0.45·36.637 = 16.49 σ); 5·λ_D = 19.0 σ no longer fits in the dry phase and would buy 9.16 % → 4.04 % at the cost of 1.85× the pair work. Reciprocal space (Ewald/PPPM) was rejected not on cost but on substance: mesh methods exist because the lattice sum of 1/r converges only conditionally; here the screen is physical (mean-field λ_D), the sum converges absolutely and exponentially, so a real-space cutoff at a multiple of λ_D gives the same accuracy without an FFT, which this engine does not have. The Wolf scheme / damped-shifted-force was rejected too: with damping α = κ it coincides with the already implemented shifted-force screened Coulomb up to a constant self-energy term, which produces no forces. What it costs. A common cutoff for the whole non-bonded interaction would have cost ~10× the pair work and required listCapacity 5000 (3.84 GB against a ceiling of 4.295 GB), so the long range lives on a separate neighbour list over titratable beads only (there are 9296 of them out of 191778, 4.85 %): its own index compaction (a deterministic sequential pass, not atomic, so that the summation order does not drift), its own list of capacity longRangeListCapacity with its own loud overflow, rebuilds at the same frequency verletList.rebuildEvery and the same drift guarantee (skin from verletList). The force term is split by radius, not moved: nonbondedSoup keeps computing it for r < interactionRange (there its completeness is guaranteed by the existing traversal), and the new pass adds exactly the remainder interactionRange ≤ r < rc_es with the same shift constants; so none of the three force paths can lose electrostatics entirely, and the sum of the two parts is checked against brute force. longRangeMaxBoxFraction = 0.45 (rank D) is the minimum-image cap with a margin below 0.5; in a box where the cap is below 4·λ_D, the cutoff is truncated by it, and the report must print how many λ_D it then covers (at 10 mM in the dry box 20.3538 this is 2.41 λ_D, with 30.7 % of the integrated interaction discarded). The list capacity is derived, not assigned, and this corrects a mistake made in this same task: the capacity was first set equal to verletList.listCapacity = 2500, with the arithmetic checked against the wet box (9296 heads in 157464 σ³ → 1154 neighbours on average, 1332 at most, measured on the predecessor's checkpoint), and the run crashed in the dry phase, where the same box is compressed to 36.637 σ and the head density is three times higher: a sphere of radius listRange = 16.7 occupies 39.7 % of the dry box, that is, ~3690 neighbours against a capacity of 2500. So the capacity is now computed from the geometry of the tightest box of the run: cap = longRangeListSafetyFactor · (4π/3)·listRange³ · (number_of_heads / min(box)³), bounded from above by the number of heads. longRangeListSafetyFactor = 1.6 (rank D) is a margin for inhomogeneity (the heads gather on the aggregate surface rather than being smeared out), chosen so that the measured maximum of 1332 against the mean of 1154 (a ratio of 1.15 in the wet phase) is covered with a multiplicative margin. Overflow remains an exception, not a silent truncation; it is exactly what caught the mistake on the very first dry step, rather than in the report. Electrostatics list, measurement (task 'big-box', 2026-08-20): longRangeListSafetyFactor=1.6 is now confirmed by measurement rather than assumed. In the dry phase of the campaign (6693 heads, listRange=16.2794, uniform estimate 3414) the measurement gave max=4106, mean=3410.34, sd=217.40, p999=3985 -> max/uniform=1.2027, that is, the derived capacity of 5463 holds a margin of 1.33 times, with 0 overflows. In the wet box of the same run max=957 with the same capacity (it is derived from the densest phase, as it should be). Measurement: soup/cli/measure-neighbours.ts.

saltPhLimitation.basis:
Revised by task 'electrostatics' (2026-08-20, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/electrostatics-report.md; read it in full). represented has been switched false → true, and here is exactly what is now represented and what is not.

Represented. (1) Charge on the carboxyl head: a deprotonated head carries −e, and this is a per-particle dynamic state, not a property of the species. (2) Screened Coulomb repulsion between charged heads: Debye–Hückel with a shifted force, cut off at the already existing non-bonded cutoff of 2.7224620 σ. (3) Ionic strength as a real parameter: it sets the Debye length λ_D = 0.304 nm/√(I[M]), so 10 mM and 100 mM are two different interactions, not two labels. (4) pH as a real parameter: the fraction of deprotonated heads is sampled by constant-pH Monte Carlo with dG = kT·ln10·(pKa_intrinsic − pH) + dU_es, the state changes during the run, and the shift of the apparent pKa at a crowded charged surface therefore emerges from dU_es rather than being written in.

Not represented (this remains a limitation, and it is by construction, not an oversight). (a) No explicit H⁺ and no titration of the medium: pH is an external constant of the run, a crowded surface cannot locally deplete protons, and there is no buffer capacity. (b) No explicit Na⁺/Cl⁻: screening is a mean-field length, not particles, so ion condensation, charge inversion and specific ion effects (the lyotropic series) cannot be expressed. (c) No COOH···COO⁻ hydrogen bond: the polarPolar level stays 0 and is not touched by this task, so the acid-soap dimer is not inserted as a species and can show up only as a charge-alternation correlation, which is measured separately and reported separately. (d) The cutoff at 2.72 σ at 10 mM (λ_D = 3.80 σ) cuts the interaction off at 49 % of the unscreened magnitude, so the low-salt arm is underestimated and the measured pKa shift between 10 and 100 mM is a lower bound. (e) The σ → nm mapping is not calibrated: σ ∈ [0.65, 1.00] nm, and this is a factor of 1.886 on the contact repulsion of two charged heads. (f) Electrostatics does not enter the Metropolis for bond formation/break (even before this task it used only the energyKT of its rule). (g) Gate 5 (data/literature.json) is now checked by the model rather than copied from the literature, but it is checked on this model's own pH scale, whose pKa_intrinsic is monomeric (4.9), not interfacial, so the position of the window on the absolute pH scale cannot be compared with 7–9 directly; what is comparable is the shape of the window and the measured shift.

Correction (task 'long-range-electrostatics', 2026-08-20): the first version of this section shared the cutoff with the Lennard-Jones non-bonded interaction (2.7224620 σ), because of which 84 % of the integrated interaction was discarded at 10 mM and the measured salt shift of the apparent pKa came out at −0.124 against the literature's ~0.7. Electrostatics now has its own cutoff, a multiple of the Debye length (electrostatics.longRangeDebyeLengths, item 12 of its basis), the same in number of λ_D in all salt arms. What is represented and what is not is given below, unchanged.

History (task 'broth-composition', 2026-08-18, for context, now wrong in substance): "This engine carries no electrostatics: no partial charges, no Debye screen, no explicit Na+/Cl-, no Henderson-Hasselbalch protonation. Ionic strength and pH are therefore not representable, neither explicitly nor through a surrogate." The temptation to approximate the window with a surrogate (varying the energyKT of the C-O bond as a function of a "pseudo-pH") is still not implemented and remains forbidden: what was added above is not a pH surrogate but a charge with a protonation equilibrium, in which pH enters where thermodynamics says it should.

clay.surfaceChemistryBasis:
task 'clay-surface-chemistry' (2026-08-19, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/clay-surface-chemistry-report.md; read it in full). Why two limits rather than one choice. Real montmorillonite is charged, and charge cannot be represented in this engine at all (clay.basis §2), so neither of these two limits is the mineral: the hydrophilic one (P5) is the upper bound of wettability, and the apolar one (SC6/C1) is the uncharged siloxane limit from a published CG model. The honest claim is the bracket between them, so both remain selectable and both are measured with the same four measurements against the same zero. It is switched by the field clay.surfaceChemistry (or CreateSoupOpts.claySurfaceChemistry for a single run); an unknown name throws an exception rather than falling back to the default, because a silently wrong surface is exactly the error that a measurement would later attribute to physics.

Which limit is kept as the default and why that one (decision of task 'clay-surface-chemistry', 2026-08-19). The default remains hydrophilic, and this is not inertia but two arguments. (1) The literature on the real mineral: Sposito et al., PNAS 1999, 96:3358 states directly that the basal surface of smectite is hydrophilic owing to the layer charge and the hydrated exchangeable cations, and that it is specifically the uncharged analogue (pyrophyllite) that is hydrophobic; Hanczyc et al., Science 2003, 302:618 works with montmorillonite dispersed in water. Real charged montmorillonite is therefore closer to the hydrophilic limit, and the apolar limit is the pyrophyllite bound, that is, the "charge removed" limit. (2) The measurement gave no grounds for a reversal: the apolar limit does make the contact layer hydrocarbon (98 %) and barely slows growth, but it does not nucleate assembly at all (the fraction of aggregates in the 2σ band is exactly 0.000 in 11 of 11 runs, farther from the surface than any other arm), and the condition for reversing the default was precisely "concentrates carbon and nucleates assembly". Neither limit nucleates assembly at the surface, so the choice of default is decided by the literature on the mineral, not by a win in the measurement. Both limits remain selectable, and any claim about a "clay effect" in this model must be stated as a bracket.

hydrophilic.basis: Upper bound of hydrophilicity, rank D: this is a mapping (a choice), not a measured property of the mineral. Mineral → P5, the most polar uncharged bead of MARTINI 2.1; the pairs are taken as levels.mineralSolvent (P5-P4, 5.6), mineralPolar (P5-Na, 5.0), mineralApolar (P5-C1, 2.0), mineralMineral (P5-P5, 5.6), each with its own line from martini_v2.1.itp next to the number. The charged Q types are unavailable (see clay.basis §2), so P5 is the most hydrophilic surface expressible without electrostatics: a stand-in for a basal surface decorated with hydrated exchangeable cations. Exchange gain F(X) = eps(K,X) + eps(W,W) − eps(K,W) − eps(W,X): F(head)=+0.114 eps, F(tail)=−0.171 eps. Measured by task 'clay-surface' (n=10 per arm, box 30, 20000 steps): water 1.29× in the dense layer, heads 1.79×, carbon 0.21× (depleted 4.7×), donor 0.32×; chain growth cc_bond 197.7±14.2 against 277.9±19.3 without clay (t=10.6, −29%); termination co_bond 14.0±5.5 against 15.6±6.3 (t=0.60, within the scatter); aggregates move away from the surface (9.2σ against 7.6σ, band fraction 0.04 against 0.13 with uniform 0.133). That is, this limit concentrates water and heads and pushes out organics and assembly. Re-measured by task 'clay-surface-chemistry' on 11 seeds with the same code as the apolar limit (the predecessor's numbers reproduced in sign and in order of magnitude): polar fraction of the contact layer 0.950 ± 0.019 (against 0.785 over the box and 0.604 ± 0.239 without clay, t=+4.78), water 1.436 ± 0.066, head 1.546 ± 0.139, carbon 0.243 ± 0.158 (t=−7.34), donor 0.317 ± 0.126; cc_bond 202.8 ± 11.4 against 266.1 ± 16.8 (−23.8 %, t=−10.36); aggregates farther than uniform (8.66 ± 1.52σ, t=+1.62) and band fraction 0.075 ± 0.058 against 0.148 ± 0.100 (t=−2.06). One discrepancy with the predecessor, stated plainly: termination here is not "within the scatter" but lower, co_bond 13.3 ± 3.2 against 20.0 ± 5.2 (−33.6 %, t=−3.63, whereas the predecessor had t=0.60 at n=10); the co/cc ratio barely changes (0.065 against 0.075 without clay), that is, there are fewer terminations because there are fewer chains to begin with, not because the surface hinders capping them with a head.

apolar.basis: Uncharged (siloxane) limit, rank C: this is how the published CG clay model maps the surface, and it is precisely this mapping that the hydrophilic limit above did not agree with (concern §1 of the 'clay-surface' report). (a) Sposito et al., PNAS 1999, 96:3358 "Surface geochemistry of the clay minerals": the basal siloxane surface is hydrophobic in itself (pyrophyllite, the uncharged analogue of montmorillonite, is hydrophobic); it is made hydrophilic by the layer charge and the hydrated exchangeable cations. (b) Khan & Goel, J. Phys. Chem. B 2019, 123:9011 (arXiv:1907.06345) and the MARTINI-3 parametrisation of phyllosilicates (arXiv:2507.06159): the basal SiO2 beads are assigned SC6, i.e. the apolar subtype of class C, while wetting is carried by charged beads (SQ5 in the octahedral layer, Q2 on the counterions), which are absent here. The mapping is therefore literal: mineral = apolar bead, and all its pairs refer to already existing rows of the apolar class: mineralSolvent→solventApolar (P4-C1, 2.0), mineralApolar→apolarApolar (C1-C1, 3.5), mineralMineral→apolarApolar, mineralPolar→polarApolar (0.0). This task introduces not a single new number: surfaceChemistry is a level alias, not a depth. Exchange gain F(head)=−0.286 eps, F(tail)=+1.286 eps (+1.17 kT at kT=1.1), i.e. the surface prefers the tail to water; the sign is opposite to that of the hydrophilic limit. Honest consequence, stated plainly: mineralPolar→polarApolar=0 means mineral-head is exactly zero, as is tail-head in this table (an existing convention of the table, not a new choice made by this task); in MARTINI 2.1 the C1-Na pair has a shallow but non-zero well, so this limit slightly overestimates the repulsion of the head. Measured by task 'clay-surface-chemistry' (n=11 shared seeds 41-44,46-52, box 30, 20000 steps, the same composition, the same null from 25 surface-free planes in the same run; full trail: .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/clay-surface-chemistry-report.md). (1) The contact layer becomes almost purely hydrocarbon: the polar fraction of the layer is 0.018 ± 0.010 versus 0.785 over the box and 0.604 ± 0.239 without clay (t=−8.13), i.e. 98 % of the layer is C and H. Water is expelled (0.005 ± 0.003 of its box average, versus 1.436 ± 0.066 at the hydrophilic limit), and the head is expelled to exactly zero in all 11 runs and over a span of ~7σ from the plane. (2) But relative to its own box average, carbon is not enriched: 0.848 ± 0.157 (donor 0.985 ± 0.104); relative to the far field (the 5 most distant bins, where the water slab sits) the contact bin gives 8.0× for C and 9.0× for H, and these are two different quantities, both reported honestly: the surface does not so much accumulate carbon as drive out water and the head, while the carbon itself collects in a broad layer at 6-10σ. (3) Growth: cc_bond 241.0 ± 15.8 versus 266.1 ± 16.8 without clay (−9.4 %, t=−3.61), i.e. the drop is three times smaller than at the hydrophilic limit; with no catalytic sites at all (siteCatalystFraction=0) the apolar sheet accelerates growth: 292.8 ± 11.9 versus 266.1 ± 16.8 (+10.0 %, t=+3.64). (4) Termination does not change: co_bond 18.4 ± 5.2 versus 20.0 ± 5.2 (t=−0.73, within the scatter). (5) Assembly does not nucleate here either, and even more so than at the hydrophilic limit: the mean aggregate distance is 10.24 ± 0.44σ versus 7.50 for a uniform distribution and 7.53 ± 1.74 without clay (t=+5.02), and the fraction within the 2σ band is exactly 0.000 in all 11 runs versus 0.148 ± 0.100 without clay. The reason, stated plainly: an amphiphile in this model must have a head, and mineralPolar is zero here, so the film on the surface is headless; concentrating hydrocarbon and nucleating assembly turned out to be different things.

clay.basis:
task 'clay-surface' (2026-08-19, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/clay-surface-report.md, read it in full). The project owner asked "make a composition similar to the original broth + add clay"; the broth was made by task 'broth-composition', the clay here.

1. Why clay, in the science (rank C: independent literature, not measured on this tree). Montmorillonite is a standard prebiotic mineral catalyst/concentrator. (a) Hanczyc, Fujikawa & Szostak, Science 2003, 302:618 "Experimental Models of Primitive Cellular Compartments" (doi:10.1126/science.1089904): montmorillonite accelerates the spontaneous conversion of fatty-acid micelles into vesicles by a factor of roughly 100 and itself ends up encapsulated inside the resulting vesicle together with adsorbed RNA. (b) Ferris & Ertem and subsequent work: Ferris, Orig. Life Evol. Biosph. 2002, 32:311 "Montmorillonite catalysis of 30-50 mer oligonucleotides" (doi:10.1023/A:1020543312109; PMID 12458736): on montmorillonite, oligomers of 40-50 units grow from 5'-phosphorimidazolides. (c) Sposito et al., PNAS 1999, 96:3358 "Surface geochemistry of the clay minerals": the basal siloxane surface is hydrophobic in itself (pyrophyllite, the uncharged analogue of montmorillonite, is hydrophobic); it is made hydrophilic by the layer charge and the hydrated exchangeable cations.

2. What this model cannot represent, stated plainly. The defining property of clay is surface charge (isomorphous substitutions in the lattice plus exchangeable cations). There is no electrostatics here at all (see saltPhLimitation), so the charge cannot be represented, neither explicitly nor by a surrogate that would look like chemistry. Direct consequence for the literature above: Ferris explicitly links the strength of catalysis to the magnitude of the negative lattice charge and the number of bound cations; this mechanism is not reproduced here, only its geometric part is imitated (a surface + a catalytic site sitting on it). Also not represented: the interlayer space (interlayer) as a quasi-two-dimensional reaction medium: the sheet here is single-layer (sheets=1), adsorption occurs onto the two basal faces, and there is no gallery between layers; encapsulation of the sheet inside a vesicle (in the model the sheet is immobile by construction and therefore cannot be captured); edge chemistry (edge sites) distinct from the basal surface (the sheet is periodic in x,y and has no edges at all).

3. Where the well depths come from (rank C for the ratios, rank A for the absolute scale). The table solvent.attractionScale.pairEpsilon is extended, not reinvented: a fourth class MINERAL and four pairs (mineralSolvent/mineralPolar/mineralApolar/mineralMineral) have been added, taken from the same file martini_v2.1.itp, with the same conversion eps=C6^2/(4*C12), with the same reference='apolarApolar'; that is, the absolute scale is still tied to the rank-A epsilon from data/params.json, and not a single kJ/mol is carried over into the energy unit of this model. Mapping: mineral surface → P5, the most polar uncharged MARTINI bead. Why exactly this, and where the uncertainty lies: the charged Q types are unavailable per item 2, so P5 is the upper bound of hydrophilicity expressible without electrostatics. This is not what the published CG clay model does, and this must be said honestly: in the MARTINI-3 parametrisation of phyllosilicates (arXiv:2507.06159; predecessor: Khan & Goel, J. Phys. Chem. B 2019, 123:9011, arXiv:1907.06345) the basal SiO2 beads are assigned SC6 (class C, i.e. the apolar subtype), while hydrophilicity is carried by charged beads (SQ5 in the octahedral layer, Q2 on the counterions), exactly the mechanism that is absent here. So our sheet is a declared hydrophilic idealisation (a stand-in for a basal surface decorated with hydrated cations), not the uncharged limit of the mineral: the uncharged limit is pyrophyllite, and it is hydrophobic (item 1(c)). Lower bound of the effect, not measured in this task: mapping the mineral to P4 (the same as water) would give exactly zero preference, and mapping it to SC6/C1 would give displacement of water from the surface.

4. Immobility is structural, not achieved through a large mass. soup/wgsl/step.wgsl's kick_drift_wrap_main and kick_thermostat_main read the per-particle flag frozenRO and, for a flagged particle, write a velocity of exactly zero and do not update the position at all; that is, the coordinate of a mineral bead cannot change under any force, at any temperature or at any dt (unlike a "heavy" particle, which drifts all the same). The flag is per-PARTICLE, not per-species, precisely because the catalytic sites on the surface are beads of the same species M as the free catalysts of the broth: part of the pool is frozen in the sheet, the rest diffuse.

5. The sheet geometry is derived, not set by a number. The sheet lattice spacing = the WCA contact distance for the mineral-mineral pair (wca_cut(sigma*(r+r)/2) from data/params.json, rank A); that is, the beads sit where the force between them goes to zero, close-packed; not a single new number. Number of beads = round(Lx/spacing) * round(Ly/spacing) with the actual spacing Lx/nx, Ly/ny (commensurate with the periodic box); this is why start has no 'K' field: the count is not part of the composition, it follows from the box. The sheet lies in the plane z = Lz/2 (the centre of the box, again not a number). Thickness: one layer of beads, radiusSigma=1.0; with the estimate sigma≈0.73-0.90 nm already recorded in solvent.basis §1, this is 0.73-0.90 nm versus 0.96 nm for the real TOT layer of montmorillonite, i.e. one bead layer is one mineral layer (agreement in order of magnitude, not a fit). Impermeability of the sheet is not claimed but measured (see the report): water at the centre of a square cell of the sheet ends up at 0.79*spacing from four beads, deep inside their WCA core.

6. Catalytic sites on the surface: the same machinery, not a second one. A site on the sheet is a bead of species M inserted into the sheet lattice and frozen; everything else (the requiresCatalyst gate of the rules, the centerLink tether with a real FENE spring, occupancy=1, maxHoldSteps, desorbStretch/desorbTimeout; see adsorption) works on it without a single change, because all this machinery addresses a particle by its species and by its index, not by its mobility. siteCatalystFraction is the fraction of the broth's catalyst pool moved onto the sheet, not added to it: the total number of M in a run with clay and without clay is the same, so the comparison of chain growth is not confounded with "there is now more catalyst". The value 0.25 is rank D, a choice: at box=30 this is 25 sites on 729 sheet positions (coverage 3.4%, i.e. isolated sites, not a continuous catalytic strip), and it leaves three quarters of the pool in the bulk. Sensitivity to this fraction was not measured (beyond the task's budget), and this is recorded, not hidden.

7. The sheet is incompatible with changing the box. applyBoxScaleOnce (soup/src/soup-box-scale.ts) throws an exception if the system contains frozen beads: affine scaling of the box would stretch the sheet lattice spacing (the sheet would no longer be close-packed) and would shift particles that by construction cannot move. Therefore areaMove/scaleBoxTo/dryWetCycle do not work with clay, and rather than silently giving a wrong answer they refuse. All measurements of area per lipid at zero tension (the bilayer gates) run without clay, which is what is required: they measure the membrane, not the mineral.

8. Added by task 'clay-surface-chemistry' (2026-08-19). (a) The excluded zone was computed from the small bead. exclusionHalfWidth was taken as the maximum over mineral-other pairs only, but the catalytic site in the sheet is a bead of species M, the largest in the file (radiusSigma 1.2 versus 1.0 for the mineral). A mobile catalyst could start at 1.2347σ from the plane, i.e. inside the WCA core of the site (1.3470σ): a cold overlap with a bead that by construction cannot move away (exactly what startBasis §2 warns about). The measured overlap energy is 0.47 eps, so with the standard 25 sites this did not show up; fixed (the maximum is taken over the radii of all beads actually placed in the sheet), excluded zone 1.2347→1.3470σ when siteCount>0. (b) The sheet is a hard wall, and some runs diverge. A bead pressed against an immobile bead receives the whole WCA impulse alone (a mobile partner would share it), and at the rank-A dt a run sometimes goes nonFinite. Measured: 1 of 43 arms with the sheet after fix (a) versus 2 of ~20 before it, and 0 of 22 arms without the sheet (frozen catalysts in the bulk: also 0), i.e. the divergence is attributed to the wall by measurement, not by guesswork. Fix (a) removed the divergence that reproduced 2 of 2 on seed 42 at site fraction 0.5, but did not remove divergence completely (seed 45, apolar limit, standard fraction, 2 of 2). A diverging run does not enter the statistics and is printed as CHEM-DIVERGED. (c) The site fraction was swept, see the report: growth falls monotonically with it (246.8 → 202.8 → 157.2 → 5.8 at 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 1.0), i.e. the clay effect on growth claimed by the predecessor is mostly a property of this number, not of the surface.

adsorption.basis:
task 'adsorption', 2026-08-17 (adsorption-report.md, diagnosis in surface-growth-report.md): the previous attempt (surface-growth) recorded the catalyst<->tip association only as bookkeeping (centerLink), without a force physically holding the pair together; thermal diffusion carried the growing end away from the centre within a few integration steps, and almost all 400 centres got permanently stuck on the very first unfinished chain (0 amphiphiles in 60000 steps, both seeds, single-bead fraction 90.5%). The fix (soup/wgsl/bond.wgsl + soup/wgsl/step.wgsl): the same bond now also carries a real FENE spring (soup/wgsl/step.wgsl's bondedForce, the same fene_dv formula as any covalent bond in this engine) between the catalyst and its current end; it physically holds the end at the surface, exactly as the task requires ('adsorption, a physical attraction, not a table entry'). This bond lives in a separate buffer (centerLink), not in bondSlots: it does not consume carbon valence and is invisible to findAmphiphiles (soup/src/amphiphile.ts reads only bonds()/bondSlots, never centerLink), which is exactly requirement 1 of the task ('must NOT count against the carbon's chain valence, and the recogniser must never treat it as part of an amphiphile').

A trap measured in the fix itself, now fixed (adsorption-report.md): the first version of the geometry check on tether creation/reattachment compared the distance against P.r_inf (the full range of the FENE bond, ~1.5σ); measured: position drift blew up to 1e4-1e9σ within a couple of hundred steps after the first such 'at the limit' claim, because fene_dv(r) grows sharply as r approaches r_inf, and a single explicit (not implicit) integrator step can jump past r_inf, where the formula changes sign. The fix is not new physics but the same principle that already holds for covalent bonds: every bond in this file forms at the reactive contact distance (wca_cut(bPairB(...))≈1.1-1.25σ, substantially below r_inf), not at the limit. Both tether creation points (nucleation, reattachment on elongation) are now checked against exactly this distance: soup/wgsl/bond.wgsl's propagateOnCenter, full analysis in the comments there.

Second trap, measured and fixed (adsorption-report.md): the first version of desorbTimeout fully released centerLink and in no way marked that this chain end had once been growing (unlike an end that simply never nucleated), whereas propagateOnCenter's own elongation logic and terminateOnCenter both require an owner (owner != BOND_NONE), so an end desorbed without termination became forever neither growing nor terminable; measured: 1108-1110 timeout desorptions versus 1-6 real terminations in 60000 steps (two seeds), i.e. the deadlock valve itself became the main cause of chain death. The fix is re-adsorption: propagateOnCenter now allows that an ownerless chain end (owner==BOND_NONE) is not only a 'permanently inert far end' but also, equally plausibly in physical terms, an intermediate desorbed in the middle of growth, and lets a free catalyst nearby adopt it anew as its own new end (the same reactive contact distance at claim time, the same claim-then-rollback as everywhere else in this file). The model does not distinguish these two cases structurally (both are 'one existing contact, no owner') and does not try to: the task's 'released into solution... freeing the centre' describes precisely a desorbed intermediate that is actually given a chance to be picked up by another centre rather than being guaranteed to die.

occupancy=1 was considered (requirement 5 of the task) and deliberately kept, not inherited by default: a real catalytic particle (data/soup.json's monomer 'M', radiusSigma=1.2, larger than carbon) in this crude-grained model already represents many real atomic centres folded into one particle for the purposes of this level of detail; supporting several simultaneous chains per particle would require remaking centerLink from a single u32 slot into an array modelled on bondSlots, with its own claim/release discipline for each slot, a separate structural change that the task explicitly ranks lower in priority than the deadlock fix ('the deadlock fix matters more than the occupancy number'). The deadlock was caused by the absence of a force, not by occupancy=1 as such (surface-growth-report.md §4 blames precisely the absence of the tether; occupancy=1 was only what made the effect total), so after this fix occupancy=1 is a physically meaningful choice: one active site serves one growing chain at a time and is freed after its termination/desorption for the next one, a Fischer-Tropsch idealisation at this level of detail, not an artificial limit on throughput.

maxHoldSteps=30000 was recomputed from a measurement, not picked by eye (the first attempt was 6000, withdrawn by its own measurement): a diagnostic run (box 50σ, C:12000 O:4000 H:12000 M:400, kT=1.1, seed=19, adsorption-report.md) gave 3827 cc_bond events in 60000 steps with 400 catalysts, i.e. the mean real time between two consecutive successful propagation events on one centre ≈ 400*60000/3827 ≈ 6270 steps. With the original maxHoldSteps=6000 (less than this mean!), for a Poisson process with such a mean interval P(no event within T=6000) = exp(-6000/6270) ≈ 0.38: the valve fired in ~38% of all 'quiet' intervals even for a centre that is actually working at the normal rate, which explains the measured 1108-1110 firings (the valve became the dominant release mechanism, not a rare safety net). The new value is 5x the measured mean interval (30000≈5*6270, rounded): at T=30000 the same formula gives P(no event) = exp(-30000/6270) ≈ exp(-4.79) ≈ 0.0083, i.e. less than 1% false firings on a normally working centre, and at the same time half of this task's step budget (60000), so the guarantee 'deadlock is impossible by construction' remains empirically testable within a single run, not merely claimed. An event is either a successful propagation or a termination on this centre (both reset the centerHeldSteps counter: soup/wgsl/bond.wgsl's propagateOnCenter/terminateOnCenter); exceeding the limit releases the centre regardless of distance (soup/wgsl/bond.wgsl's desorbTimeout) and is counted by a separate counter (desorbEvents[1]), not as a co_bond event (it is not a completed amphiphile). A second, independent valve is desorbStretch: if the pair nevertheless stretches beyond the reactive contact distance to a distance equal to or greater than P.r_inf (data/params.json's fene.rInf, no new number), the centre releases it immediately, regardless of the timer; this is literally 'the adsorption bond is stretched beyond the bonded range' from the task. Both counters are read via SoupSystem.desorbEvents().

Remaining gap, not closed by this fix, per measurement (adsorption-report.md): even after re-adsorption and the recomputation of maxHoldSteps, co_bond remains almost never successful (2 events on seed=19 in 60000 steps versus 3827 cc_bond); termination is restricted only to held/tethered ends (soup/wgsl/bond.wgsl's terminateOnCenter), i.e. to a population of ~400-500 particles locally confined by the spring near their catalyst, rather than all 12000 carbons in the bulk, as was the case when co_bond.attemptRate was calibrated in kinetic-growth-report.md (that calibration did not know about the later catalyst-gating of termination; that was only added in surface-growth). The ratio k_p/(k_p+k_t) remains arithmetically valid only if the opportunity frequency is equal for both sides; here it is again not equal, now for a different, more precisely diagnosed reason (the reaction volume of termination has shrunk by a factor of ~25-30, not simply 'termination proceeds throughout the whole volume'). The task explicitly forbids raising co_bond.attemptRate to close this gap numerically; see adsorption-report.md for the full analysis and the honestly unverified conclusion on tails 12-18.

dryWetCycle.basis:
task 'wet-dry-cycle', 2026-08-17, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/wet-dry-cycle-report.md. Experimental basis, rank D (an engineering implementation of a measured mechanism, not a literature constant): every run before this task kept volume/temperature/concentration constant throughout, and the best such run (box 46, 46600 particles, 300000 steps) gave 682 amphiphiles in a single aggregate, a curved bilayer dome whose edge stays open (adding material widens the dome rather than closing it). The experimentally proven route to closed fatty-acid vesicles is drying-rehydration (Deamer and co-workers: drying forces the amphiphiles into lamellar stacks; rehydration makes the stacks swell and bud off closed vesicles). The mechanical work of closure comes from the change of conditions, not from the membrane alone; this file adds exactly that change of conditions, without touching anything in the membrane/chemistry/thresholds themselves.\n\nenabled=false: this mechanism is off by default. soup/src/sim.ts's createSoup() reads this field, but a particular run must explicitly ask for the cycle (CreateSoupOpts.dryWetCycle=true), or this file itself must be edited to true; no existing test/viewer/regression, and no run without that request, sees any difference in behaviour relative to the code before this task.\n\ntargetDryDensity=0.6 is the amplitude, chosen from the density scale this project has already measured, not by eye: box=34 (density ~0.72 particles/sigma^3 with the data/soup.json's start composition) was measured as runaway polymerisation (almost all the carbon in a handful of very long chains, no amphiphiles; verletList.basis's own analysis), and box 40-50 (density ~0.45-0.48) is the working dilute regime, where the 682-molecule dome was obtained (46600/46^3=0.4789). 0.6 lies strictly between these two measured boundaries, with an almost equal margin on either side (0.6-0.45=0.15 against the upper failure boundary of runaway polymerisation; 0.72-0.6=0.12 of margin below it): far enough above the 'dilute' regime to actually force packing (not a micro-nudge), but with a deliberate margin below the measured threshold of breakdown into runaway polymerisation. soup/src/sim.ts's createSoup() derives the dry box from this density and the system's own N/wetBox (dryVolume=N/targetDryDensity), not from a literal box size, so the same number reproduces the same physical density whatever box/composition the caller requested.\n\nperiodSteps=50000, dryFraction=0.5, cycles=5: the period and the number of cycles, chosen by the task budget, not by physics. The hard rule of this task is a single foreground call (foreground), no background, at most ~600 s per call; at the speed measured for this engine, 400-1000 steps/s, this limits one run to roughly 300000 steps. 5 cycles of 50000 steps (25000 wet + 25000 dry each) give 250000 steps: under the ceiling, with headroom for grid/Verlet-list rebuilds and for measuring aggregates after each cycle, and enough cycles (5) to see the trajectory of the cavity across cycles rather than a single point. dryFraction=0.5 gives equal weight to the concentration and rehydration phases, the simplest unbiased choice (there is no measurement favouring one phase over the other). Explicitly against a longer dry arm (the task directly warns against taking the dry phase to a new steady state): 25000 steps per arm is a small fraction of even one full 300000-step run up to the vector dome, so the dry phase remains a transient peak compression, not a second steady-state point.\n\nrampSteps=6, rampRelaxSteps=200: the box change is not an instantaneous jump. It is spread over 6 log-linear box increments (soup/src/sim.ts's applyBoxScale), each followed by 200 steps of ordinary dynamics before the next one. This is the same discipline that engine/src/sim.ts's area move already applies to its own trial steps (AREA_MOVE_LOG_DELTA=0.012 per single trial), generalised from a stochastic MC step (with rejection) to a forced mechanical one (without rejection, so each increment must be small in itself rather than relying on Metropolis rejection as insurance against WCA overlap). With the target linear factor for the transition box46->targetDryDensity's equivalent (see the report for the actual numbers of a particular run), 6 increments keep the log step per increment of the same order as the already validated area move step size, and with 200 relaxation steps between them, contacts compressed by one increment have time to move apart under WCA repulsion and the thermostat before the next increment. Both values are an engineering estimate (rank D), not a measured optimum; on the first run of this task they either worked or did not (the Verlet list/drift throw an exception rather than silently corrupting the data); see the report for what was actually measured.

Revised: task 'wet-dry-cycling' (2026-08-20, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/wet-dry-cycling-report.md). The reason for the revision is structural, not a matter of taste: the previous numbers were derived for a medium without explicit water (run box 20, N=3839, ro_tot=0.4799). Task 'loud-failure-and-liquid-water' brought the water up to the measured liquid threshold of 0.8 sigma^-3, and the total density of the broth became ro_tot=1.21793, above the previous targetDryDensity=0.6; that is, on real liquid water deriveCycleConfig (soup/src/soup-box-scale-math.ts) throws the exception 'the dry phase must concentrate, not dilute'. Cycling with real water is physically impossible with the old number; the new one is derived, not fitted.

targetDryDensity=1.34 sigma^-3 (rank D, measured by this task). The literature amplitude: Ross & Deamer, Life 2016, 6(3):28 (doi:10.3390/life6030028) measure evaporation as a roughly 1400-fold reduction in volume (to an equivalent monomer concentration of ~9 M) and attribute 5-10 kcal/mol of oligomer stability to crowding/excluded volume, against a condensation endergonicity of +3.3 kcal/mol. This model cannot express such a compression, and that is stated plainly: scaling the box at fixed composition compresses the water together with the organics, and close packing of unit-diameter cores lies at 1.4142 sigma^-3, so the whole available range runs from 1.21793 to <1.4142. 1.34 was chosen: the highest density at which the medium was measured to be still mobile (free carbon, MSD over 2000 steps: 0.5929 sigma^2 at 1.21793, 0.1827 at 1.28061, 0.0950 at 1.34120, 0.0720 at 1.40106, i.e. D=4.94e-3, 1.52e-3, 7.9e-4, 6.0e-4 sigma^2/tau), with a margin to close packing of 1.4142/1.3412=1.054. The actual concentration factor is 1.3412/1.21793=1.101 against the literature's 1400; that is, on the logarithm of concentration the model reproduces ln(1.101)/ln(1400)=1.3% of the evaporation. This is a limitation of the model, not a parameter, and it is recorded here so that nobody reads 1.34 as 'dry'.

cycles=6: Higgs, Life 2016, 6(2):24 (doi:10.3390/life6020024, PMC4931461): 'These limits are reached after about six cycles for the parameters illustrated'. The number of cycles is a physical parameter, so the report must give the trend across cycles, not a single convenient value.

dryFraction=0.65 is the lower end (more conservative, more wet time) of the literature range, not a fit: Higgs 2016 in his own model used t_dry=8 against t_wet=0.5 (fraction 0.94); the experimental protocol of Rieder et al., ACS Cent. Sci. 2025 (doi:10.1021/acscentsci.5c00488, PMC12464751) is up to 10 cycles with a step of dt=24 h, the dry state being reached in 8-10 h, i.e. a dry/wet fraction of ~0.6-0.67. 0.65 was taken.

periodSteps=32000: derived from the measured mobility, not from the budget. The dry arm must be longer than the time the compressed medium needs to rearrange over one particle diameter: at ro=1.3412 the measured D=7.9e-4 sigma^2/tau gives t(1 sigma)=1/(6D)=211 tau=21100 steps; 0.65*32000=20800 steps is exactly that scale. The wet arm, 0.35*32000=11200 steps, at the wet D=4.94e-3 gives a root-mean-square displacement of sqrt(6*4.94e-3*112)=1.82 sigma, i.e. more than a diameter: precisely the 'repositioning of the molecules' that Higgs 2016 names as the function of the wet phase ('The likely benefit of the wet phases is that they permit rearrangement of molecules and bring molecules together that may polymerize in the next dry phase').

rampSteps=6, rampRelaxSteps=200: kept, and the choice now has arithmetic instead of an estimate: the full linear compression of the transition is (1/1.101)^(1/3)=0.9678, i.e. ln=-0.0327 over 6 increments = 0.00545 per increment = 0.545% in length, against 0.6% in length for the already validated area move step (AREA_MOVE_LOG_DELTA=0.012 in ln of the area), i.e. 0.91 of its size. Checked by measurement, not by promise: a too-fast ramp (rampSteps=1, rampRelaxSteps=0) is run as a separate arm and its result is recorded in the report.

=== Task 'evaporation' (2026-08-20), .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/evaporation-report.md: real evaporation and rehydration of the solvent. ===
The predecessor (wet-dry-cycling-report.md) named the structural gap in so many words: the particle count is fixed in createSoup, so water cannot leave the system, compressing the box at constant composition compresses the water together with the organics, and the whole available amplitude is 1.1002x against ~1400x in Ross & Deamer 2016, i.e. 1.3% of the literature effect on the logarithm of concentration. The four fields below add precisely the departure of the solvent. All four are off by default via evaporateSolvent=false: the path without evaporation (pure box scaling) stays bit-for-bit the same as before this task, and tests/soup-drywet-cycling.test.ts checks exactly that path.

1. evaporateSolvent=false: rank D, the same off-by-default discipline as enabled above. A particular run asks for evaporation explicitly (CreateSoupOpts.evaporateSolvent / soup/cli/campaign.ts --evaporate). No existing test, gate, viewer or checkpoint lineage sees any difference.

2. residualSolventFraction=1/1400=0.0007142857142857143: rank A-derived, from Ross & Deamer, Life 2016, 6(3):28, doi:10.3390/life6030028: their evaporation reduced the volume of the solution roughly 1400-fold. The volume of an aqueous solution is essentially the volume of the water, so "reduce the volume 1400-fold with the organic content unchanged" maps one to one onto "remove 1 - 1/1400 of the solvent". This is not a fit and not a free parameter: the number is taken from a measurement and converted into model units by an exact relation. On box 30 (W=21600) the remainder = round(21600/1400) = 15 beads, i.e. a realised removal factor of 1440x (rounding to a whole bead is the only discrepancy from 1400x, and it is stated here, not hidden).

3. Coupling to the box, and what limits concentration. Removing water at an unchanged box lowers the total density; that is not drying. Drying reduces the volume as the water leaves, so the dry box is computed from the remaining particle count: dryBox = computeDryBox(box, N_org + W_residual, targetDryDensity), with the same field targetDryDensity=1.34 and not a single new amplitude constant. Arithmetic on box 30: N_org=11284 (C 1860 + O 7440 + H 1860 + M 124), W_residual=15, N_dry=11299, V_dry=11299/1.34=8432.09, L_dry=20.3537. The concentration factor of the organics = V_wet/V_dry = 27000/8432.09 = 3.2020x against the previous 1.1002x, i.e. ln(3.2020)/ln(1400) = 16.1% of the literature effect on the logarithm against the previous 1.3%, a 12.4-fold increase. What limits it: (a) close packing of the organic beads themselves. rho_org(dry) <= sqrt(2) = 1.4142 (the densest packing of unit-diameter cores), while rho_org(wet) = 11284/27000 = 0.41793, so the absolute ceiling of the factor = 1.4142/0.41793 = 3.3839x, and the achieved 3.2020x is 94.6% of the ceiling. (b) More importantly: the 1400x of L1 is the compression of a dilute pond, whereas our broth is already far more concentrated than that pond. The organic:water molar ratio here is (C+O)/W = 9300/21600 = 0.4306; L1 start with 0.015 M decanoate against 55.5 M water = 2.703e-4, i.e. our wet composition is already 1593 times more concentrated than the pond that L1 evaporated. Compressing that pond 1400-fold brings it to a ratio of 0.3784; that is, our wet state is already 1.14 times more concentrated than the point at which evaporation in the literature ends. Demanding 1400x here would mean rho_org = 585 sigma^-3, 414 times beyond densest packing. Hence 1400x is unattainable for this composition and meaningless as a target; what is attainable and meaningful is 3.20x of additional concentration, and it is against that figure that the chemistry is measured.

4. Which water leaves: a model choice, rank D. Solvent beads leave in index order, from the tail of the water block. This is a spatially uniform random sample, not one taken at the edge: the index of a water bead is unrelated to its position (soup/src/soup-init-state.ts hands out lattice sites with a Fisher-Yates shuffle over all sites, and after that the position is determined by diffusion). Preferential removal from the surface, which would be more honest for real drying, is not merely harder here, it is undefined: the box is fully periodic and has no free interface with air at all (see saltPhLimitation on the same device for what the model does not represent). The bias this introduces is stated plainly: (a) it is always the same subset of beads that leaves, not a fresh random sample every cycle; (b) evaporation is uniform over the volume, so the drying front and the stratification associated with it are not represented; (c) the solvent block must be the last non-empty block of the composition, otherwise truncation would shift the indices of the non-water particles; this is checked and throws, rather than silently corrupting the bond graph.

5. Where the water returns. Rehydration runs in the reverse order: first a ramped expansion of the box (organics only), then a single insertion of all the returning solvent into the already diluted organics. Inserting the water gradually while enlarging the box along the way is impossible in this model, and this is measurable: affine expansion widens every gap by the same 3.2% linearly, i.e. nowhere does it create a bead-sized cavity, and at a total density of 1.2-1.34 there are no free cavities of radius sigma in the liquid. So the insertion is done where there is room: on the wet box at rho_org=0.41793. The cost of this decision is also stated plainly: for (rampSteps-1)*rampRelaxSteps real steps of every rehydration the system runs without solvent and with a falling organic density; on box 30 this is 2200 steps out of 32000 per cycle (6.9%), and it is an artefact of the scheme, not physics.

6. insertionMinSeparationSigma=0.75: rank D, derived from the saturation of random sequential addition (RSA) of hard spheres, phi_RSA = 0.3841 (rank C, independent RSA literature, not calibrated on this tree). The volume fraction required for the entire wet pool at exclusion diameter d on box 30: N*(pi/6)*d^3/V = 32884*0.523599*d^3/27000 = 0.63800*d^3. The largest admissible d = (0.3841/0.63800)^(1/3) = 0.8445 sigma; 0.75 sigma was taken, which gives phi = 0.2692, a margin of 1.427x to saturation. 0.75 sigma lies inside the repulsive WCA core (water-water contact = sigma), so the insertion must be followed by minimisation; see 7.

7. Minimisation after insertion moves only the inserted beads. The number of iterations is not a field of this file but a derived value: ceil(2*(wcaCutoff(largest pair involving the solvent) - insertionMinSeparationSigma*sigma) / (coldStartRelax.maxDisplacementSigma*sigma)); the bound on the total displacement of a normalised descent is d0*(it+1)/2, and this is the requirement "enough to lift an insertion from 0.75 sigma to the outer WCA radius". On these numbers = ceil(2*(1.23474-0.75)/0.1) = 10 iterations. During this minimisation all previously existing particles are marked as immobile (the same frozen flag as the mineral sheet has), so rehydration physically cannot repack what formed in the dry phase: the positions of the non-water particles are bit-for-bit the same before and after insertion, and this is checked by measurement, not by promise. This also disposes of the objection "minimisation in the middle of a trajectory anneals the structure": there is nothing to anneal, only the 21585 new solvent beads move.

8. evaporationRampSteps=12: rank D. The total box change with evaporation is much larger than without it (|ln(30/20.3537)| = 0.38794 against 0.03184 for the path without evaporation), so a ramp of 6 increments would give 6.3% linear per increment. 12 increments give an ln-step of 0.032328, i.e. 3.181% linear: exactly the scale that the predecessor measured as safe as a single instantaneous jump (its §4.4: a single jump of 3.2% linear at rho_tot 1.218->1.34, boxes 20 and 30, zero non-finite components, zero Verlet-list overflows, zero bond-length violations). rampRelaxSteps=200 was not changed.

9. Correction to item 8, measured in this same task: evaporationRampSteps 12 -> 18. The justification for the number 12 ("3.2% linear: exactly the jump the predecessor measured as safe") turned out to be incomplete: that measurement was made on a system in which nothing had assembled yet. As soon as the material had aggregated (from the second cycle onwards on box 30), affine compression by 3.18% per increment leaves residual force peaks of 0.9e3-2.7e3 (measured per increment, the [evaporation] lines in the report), and the relaxation steps of the ramp diverged three times: assertVerletSafety threw drifts of 2.98e7, 2.13e14 and 3.71e8 sigma while the state was finite, i.e. this is a genuine physical blow-up, not Inf. The cause is established by arithmetic, not by guesswork: the integrator is stable as long as the force does not change substantially within one step, and for the WCA r^-12 core the force changes by a factor of e over dr = r/13, so the stability bound is F <= sigma/(13*dt^2) = 1.0/(13*0.0001) = 769 in these units, which is below the measured peaks. 18 increments give an ln-step of 0.021552 (2.13% linear). In addition, a guard is kept: after every increment max|F| is measured, and if it exceeds the same derived bound sigma/(13*dt^2), the same minimisation (soup/src/soup-relax.ts) is run for the derived number of iterations. How many times the guard fired is printed for each increment and given in the report, because minimisation in the middle of a trajectory is a perturbation, not free insurance.
