headPlacement.basis:
Rank D, a model constraint, not a measured constant: in real chemistry the carboxyl head sits on the terminal carbon of the chain, not in the middle (a middle atom of the chain simply has no free valence for a functional group without breaking the chain). Before this switch, co_bond and cc_bond were independent with respect to the bonding site, even though valence (data/soup.json's cc_bond/co_bond, soup/wgsl/bond.wgsl's tryClaimSlot) already correctly limited how many bonds per atom (2 C-C + 1 C-O), so a head could legally settle in the middle of a chain (degree 3: 2 C-C + 1 C-O), valid by valence but not an amphiphile, because it is not terminal. Measurement (valence-and-heads-report.md, 45000 steps, kT=1.1): the fraction of bonded heads at the chain end fell from 42.7% to 32.8% when there were more heads; increasing the number of heads only increased the competition for a free head slot at the moment of encounter, regardless of whether that carbon later grows to a second C-C bond; this is a kinetic cause, not a compositional one, and adding heads does not cure it. terminalOnly=true makes 'head at the end' a condition of the bonding attempt itself (via the same atomic claim+rollback as valence), not a new energy/temperature/stage threshold. terminalOnly=false reproduces the behaviour before this change bit-for-bit: an A/B control point, like the other switches in this file. 

chainCapacity=2 (task 'two-tails', 2026-08-17) raises the head's valence, counted in tails, from 1 to 2, via the same atomic claim+rollback (soup/wgsl/bond.wgsl's tryClaimSlot, role==2), not via a new energy. Physics: the shape of an aggregate is determined by the packing parameter (tail volume against head area multiplied by tail length); a cone-shaped molecule (bulky head, one short tail) prefers a spherical/cylindrical micelle; a cylinder-shaped molecule (head area comparable to the tail cross-section) prefers a bilayer. A measurement on a dilute run (box 50σ, 28400 particles at particleScale=2, 200000 steps, .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/per-aggregate-report.md-style analysis) with chainCapacity=1 gave the micelles stage: the largest aggregate (438 amphiphiles) is a wormlike cylindrical micelle (λ0/λ2=0.085, λ1/λ2=0.230, both small: a rod, not a disc), the rest (114-124 amphiphiles) are nearly spherical (0.61-0.65 and 0.68-0.92), and there is 1 radial head layer everywhere (head outside, tail inside), exactly what the packing parameter predicts for a cone (one head bead + one short tail = cone). Two tails per head, the geometry of real membrane lipids (two acyl tails per glycerol head), turns the cone into a cylinder without changing energy/temperature/stage thresholds. This also agrees with gate 5 of the project specification (data/literature.json area-per-lipid, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-protocell-genesis-design.md §6 'pH and salt window'): single-chain fatty acids form a bilayer only when the protonated and ionised molecules pair up near the apparent pKa, i.e. a single-chain molecule physically needs a partner to imitate the geometry of two tails; chainCapacity=2 gives this same geometry directly, with one head for two tails, without separate protonation chemistry (beyond this rung of the model). Reversibility: releasePartnerSlot (bond.wgsl) already searches for the matching slot across any of the partner's 3 slots, regardless of whether it holds the first or the second tail; the break of each C-O bond uses the same co_bond/co_break pair with the same energyKT as before, so raising the ceiling does not change the forward/backward ratio for any bond, it only adds a reachable second slot. chainCapacity=1 reproduces the behaviour before this change bit-for-bit, the same A/B principle as for terminalOnly. The architectural ceiling is 3 (soup/src/sim.ts's bondSlots0, 3 slots per particle for any monomer species); the value here is read by soup/src/rules.ts's assertRulesConsistent and cannot go outside this range.

bondAttemptInterval.basis: Performance, not physics: bond_form_main/bond_break_main measured at ~42% of the full step (0.69 of 1.64 ms at N=13100, 30^3, see perf-report.md); what dominates is not the accept/reject itself but the 3x3x3 walk of the grid neighbourhood on every step for the sake of events that are rare (attemptProbability=attemptRate*dt=0.05*0.01=0.0005 per attempt). Batching k attempts into one with attemptRate*k preserves the mean attempt rate per real step (Poisson thinning, valid as long as attemptRate*dt*k is much less than 1: at k=20 this is 0.01, still a x100 margin) and does not touch acceptanceProbability = exp(-energyKT/kT), the only number that encodes detailed balance, so the forward/backward ratio is invariant to k. k=20 was chosen as the first tested point, empirically verified (perf-report.md): 3 seeds, 5000 steps, kT=1.1, mean number of bonds 1408.7±30.1 at k=20 versus 1406.7±28.3 at k=1 (difference less than one sigma); do not increase without re-verifying equilibrium empirically.

Both fields are kept in StageEvidence as diagnostics (they do not unlock a stage); the ladder now reads soup/src/aggregates.ts's analyzeAggregates(): a clustering of the same amphiphile participants by the same cutoff (minimum image, minimum-image), but per connected component, not only the largest one; for the largest few it measures the radius of gyration + three principal moments (shape), heads-versus-tails along the radial/transverse profile relative to the aggregate's own centre (not the box's), and closure via a fill inside its own bounding region (not the whole box). 

minAmphiphilesPerAggregate=13 is derived, not tuned: the number of amphiphiles needed to cover a sphere of radius 'one tail length' at the measured area per lipid. 'One tail length' = the own WCA contact radius of a single carbon bead of this broth (wcaCutoff(sigma·radiusSigma_C) = 2^(1/6)·1.0·1.0 ≈ 1.1225σ); it was chosen instead of the emergent length of the recognised chains (mode 1 carbon, pilot data/startBasis), since that length is a result of the run, not a constant on which a threshold should be built. The area per lipid is the midpoint of the already literature-calibrated range of the area-per-lipid gate (data/literature.json, Cooke & Deserno 2005, rank A, [1.1,1.5]σ², midpoint 1.3σ²). N_min = ceil(4π·1.1225²/1.3) = ceil(12.179) = 13. soup/src/aggregates.ts's derivedMinAmphiphilesPerAggregate() recomputes this same formula from scratch; soup/src/stages.ts's loadStageThresholds() throws an error on a mismatch with this number, the same technique already applied to enclosedVolume/closure.target.min. 

minMicelleAggregates=2 is about multiplicity: the micellar stage is by definition several discrete aggregates, not one; 2 is the smallest number that distinguishes this from a single dominant blob (which the old aggregationLow wrongly took for micelles, and which the synthetic test 'single percolating blob' in tests/soup-aggregates.test.ts is required not to read as micelles). 

minAmphiphileShareInAggregates=0.5 is a simple majority: a 'micelles' reading must not count if a couple of small qualifying aggregates exist while the bulk of the amphiphiles is still free/in undersized pairs; >50% of the material must really sit in objects, not merely the aggregate count ticking this box. 

lamellarFlatnessRatio=0.35/lamellarInPlaneSymmetryMin=0.5 are based on the ratios of the principal moments of inertia of the gyration tensor (ascending λ0<=λ1<=λ2): for a sphere all three are roughly equal (λ0/λ2≈1); for a flat layer (bilayer patch) λ0 << λ1≈λ2 (thin in one direction, stretched equally in the other two); for a rod/fibre λ0≈λ1 << λ2 (thin in two directions). 0.35 is a generous band above a true sphere (λ0/λ2=1): a 3-fold elongation of the plane against the thickness gives a ratio of areas/squared lengths of ~1/9≈0.11, so 0.35 rejects only a mildly flattened spheroid, not a true sphere; 0.5 for λ1/λ2 requires the two large moments to be within 2x of each other (otherwise the object is also elongated within its own 'plane' and approaches a rod, not a sheet). Both are rank D, an engineering estimate, in the same way that aggregationLow/High were before. 

aggregateHeadDensityBins=10/aggregateMinHeadsPerBin=2: the same Poisson-noise logic as headDensityBins/minHeadsPerBin, but at the scale of a single aggregate rather than the whole box: minAmphiphilesPerAggregate=13 amphiphiles over 60 bins gives ~0.2 heads/bin, well below any meaningful threshold, so with the box-wide bins/minHeadsPerBin the check for two head layers would be structurally unreachable for any aggregate of reasonable size. 10 bins, for an aggregate typical of a real wall (hundreds of amphiphiles), gives a bin width of the order of 1-1.5σ, enough to resolve the wall thickness within the headPeakSeparationMin/Max band (2-10σ, the same band as the box-wide diagnostics; the physical meaning of wall thickness is the same for flat and curved geometry). minHeadsPerBin=2 (not 10) is deliberately softer than the box-wide threshold: this analysis is already applied only to aggregates that made the detailAggregateCount cut by size, so it does not have to guard against tiny transient dimers at the same cost as the box-wide diagnostics over the whole broth. 

detailAggregateCount=5: 'the largest few', literally the wording of the task: an aggregate that is a candidate for bilayer/vesicle by construction holds most of the system's material and physically cannot be a small aggregate, so a full analysis (gyration tensor + profiles + local fill) of the five largest does not miss a real candidate, yet does not spend that cost on every transient cluster of size 2-3.

coldStartRelax.basis:
Rank D, a numerical cold-start protocol, not a physical constant: this section does not enter any force, reaction rate, threshold or corridor; it only brings the initial coordinates into a local minimum before step 1 (soup/src/soup-relax.ts throws an error when globalStep != 0, so the minimisation structurally cannot get inside the trajectory over which the measurements are computed). Task 'loud-failure-and-liquid-water' (2026-08-20), full analysis: .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/loud-failure-and-liquid-water-report.md.

Why. The initial lattice (soup/src/soup-init-state.ts, jitterFrac=0.15) gives a minimum gap of (1-2*0.15)*spacing = 0.7*spacing; at a total density of 0.8 σ⁻³ the lattice spacing is 0.8^(-1/3)=1.077 σ, i.e. a gap of 0.754 σ, which is smaller than the catalyst-catalyst contact distance (σ*(1.2+1.2)/2 = 1.2 σ). Such pairs start at roughly 40% of the depth of the repulsive core, and 1/r^13 at that depth gives a force spike that the integrator with the dt from data/params.json cannot digest. This blow-up was measured four times: ρ_tot=0.933 loudly (drift 24.58 σ in 10 steps), and ρ_tot=0.8444 / 0.75 / 0.80 silently, 68049 / 60495 / 366282 non-finite components, with an outwardly normal progress line. This is not a property of water: pure water at 0.8 σ⁻³ runs stably, because its own lattice is laid out exactly at its own spacing; the instability is specific to a mixture of different radii on a shared lattice.

What exactly is done. Normalised steepest descent with a displacement cap (soup/wgsl/relax.wgsl): in one iteration every mobile particle moves by exactly maxDisplacementSigma*sigma along its own force, and the cap decays linearly to zero over iterations iterations (without the decay, normalised descent does not converge but circles the minimum forever on an orbit with a radius of the order of the step). The force is exactly the same as in the real steps (encodeSoupForceList/encodeSoupForce): no soft core and no different dt is introduced, so after the function returns no mechanism remains that could be 'switched on' during a measured step. Velocities are not touched (the Maxwell-Boltzmann draw is kept), the step counter does not move, no PRNG stream is consumed, no bond is attempted.

The values are measured. The tuning was driven by two observables (max|F| after minimisation and the stability of the subsequent run) on the full broth composition at a total density that, before this task, had been measured as diverging; the table of measurements is in §3 of the report. Both numbers are protocol numbers (how many iterations and what maximum step): they cannot change the equilibrium distribution that the subsequent Langevin dynamics samples, only the starting point of the trajectory.

checkpoint.basis: Resumability of a long run (task 'checkpoint-resume', .superpowers/sdd/2026-08-16-soup-to-vesicle/checkpoint-resume-report.md): four real crashes of this project on one and the same full run (250000 steps, 93200 particles) had nothing to do with physics: the test's own 30-minute timeout, the page crashing while passing coordinates as a JSON array of numbers after 250000 steps had been computed correctly, puppeteer's protocolTimeout on a single evaluate, and, earlier in the project, more than a dozen background runs lost when the parent turn ended. everySteps is not a physical constant but an engineering choice of the interval between save points: it must be much smaller than the intervals that actually killed a run (tens of minutes), so that a crash loses no more than one interval of recomputation rather than the whole run; soup/cli/campaign.ts accepts --every and overrides this value with an argument when needed (the same principle as bondAttemptInterval.steps: a number in the data, with a written justification, not a literal in soup/src). dir is gitignored (.gitignore): checkpoints are the working files of a run, not code and not configuration.
